paragraphs.text: Madam President, when dictators cooperate to weaken us, we as liberal democracies have to cooperate even closer. We have to combat the enemies of our democracy outside and inside the European Union. They exist, and we know it. We have to tell people that populists and autocrats are a risk for our security, for our prosperity, for our democracy, for our freedom of expression, and for our freedom of the press.

This is why our top priority for the next years will be to protect European citizens. We will protect European citizens offline and online. The relation between citizens and technology in Europe needs to work for the citizens. We have to put technology to work for the people, not put people to work for technology. We shall invest in artificial intelligence because artificial intelligence makes people more productive. But on the other side, social networks make people less productive. Citizens shall not be tools for technology, technology shall be a tool for people to be more productive.

To make the relation between citizens and technology fair, we as the European Parliament propose a digital levy on technology giants. The European Parliament is very strongly united on using this digital levy as an own resource for the budget of the European Union. This means that we will be more able to invest in security and competitiveness and in research to support our farmers and our regions.

The choice is clear: either the richest people on earth, who own the technology giants, pay a fair share for their access to the European single market, or we might have to cut funding for farmers, researchers, for our security. I strongly believe that cuts for farmers would be a mistake. So let us work together for a strong budget based on own resources for a strong Europe.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, let me start by agreeing, President von der Leyen: Europe is strong. But when we are confronted with bullies on the geopolitical stage today – think about Trump, think about Xi Jinping – we have seen a Commission and a Council that did not react from strength but from fear. That must change.

Yes, we need a credible trade strategy and we support the work of the Commission done on the trade deals with Australia, Indonesia and India. But bilateral agreements alone will not protect us from illegal tariffs and unfair trade practices.

We welcome today Prime Minister Carney and are very much looking forward to his speech. As leader, he stood up for Canadian workers and industries. Let that be an example for all of us. And let us build further on trade and a really good coalition with Canada, the UK, Japan, Australia and others, and develop a real and coordinated response to any economic coercion and economic cheating.

We have given you, Commission, a powerful trade defence and anti-coercion toolbox. Please use it when necessary. Because bullies may not act when you lift a finger, but they will understand you when you raise a fist.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame von der Leyen, je vous entendais ici-même, il y a cinq ans, presque jour pour jour, dire exactement le contraire de tout ce que vous nous avez proposé aujourd'hui. Vous étiez à l'époque dans l'obsession idéologique des énergies renouvelables en refusant le nucléaire, vous en faites désormais la promotion. Vous nous imposiez le pacte vert et son avalanche de normes qui affaiblissent nos industries et nos agriculteurs, vous ne parlez plus aujourd'hui que de simplification.

Cette lucidité dont il est urgent qu'elle passe de la parole aux actes, est la démonstration avant tout des errements et des échecs des politiques que vous avez menées jusque-là et qui aboutissent au déclassement de l'Europe, dans tous les domaines, sur la scène mondiale. Mais là où vous ne changez pas, c'est la fuite en avant. Toujours plus de centralisme bruxellois. La construction d'un État continental qui rogne sur les libertés des choix des États membres. Après la dette commune, vous voulez des ressources propres, c'est-à-dire des impôts européens s'ajoutant à la fiscalité nationale déjà écrasante.

Et cerise sur le gâteau, ou plutôt sur le mille-feuille bureaucratique, vous voulez créer un Conseil de sécurité européen élargi à l'Ukraine, au Royaume-Uni et même au Canada. À l'inflation normative, ajoutons donc l'inflation institutionnelle. N'avez-vous pas le sentiment du ridicule alors que l'Union européenne est si faible, si peu attractive aujourd'hui, qu'un petit Européen comme l'Islande, de moins de 400 000 habitants, vient de vous claquer la porte au nez en refusant tout processus d'adhésion à l'Union européenne?

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Minister Byrne, President von der Leyen, in this envelope, addressed to the European Union and all the Member States, I have all the bills for all the programmes that we all consider crucial for the future of our Union. Let us go through a few of them: decarbonisation – hundreds of billions a year; competitiveness – hundreds of billions of euros a year; defence – hundreds of billions of euros a year. There are many more bills like this. I will not bore you. But unless we grow, we all know we cannot afford this. And to grow, we don't just have to continue to simplify – and, by the way, companies do not feel the simplification yet. We do not just have to complete the single market – which, by the way, includes not excluding EU Inc. from all sectors and all companies, and also includes completing the savings and capital markets union to liberate EUR 2 or 3 trillion of European savings to finance change. We also need to face another bill: the bill – and a large bill – for AI, because it is obvious that we cannot grow if we remain a mere spectator in the AI revolution. We are fully aware of the existence of existential warnings from the insiders, but as outsiders now, we are not even part of that discussion and we will not be able to pay the bills. And you know what happens when you don't pay the bills. And that's all.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, President von der Leyen, in an increasingly unstable world where tech bros are spreading fear and chaos, the people and businesses of Europe are longing for stable leadership.

On AI, if Europe is racing, I want to know where we are going. Will our approach on AI protect people? Will it make us more or less dependent on foreign companies? And will you ensure the race does not just pay for new tech-bro bunkers that guzzle water and energy and harm our nature?

I'm glad you are finally taking on the manipulation machines we are all carrying in our pockets, but if we only kick children off the platforms and fail to fundamentally change how these platforms work, Musk and Zuckerberg will pop champagne and leave all our health, safety and democracy at risk.

President, you promised to make all online services safe for all, everyone and our democracies. We will hold you to it. Ban addictive design in a strong Digital Fairness Act. Then we determine the rules of the game, and not AI billionaires.

paragraphs.text: Señoras presidentas, nuestros enemigos están poniendo a prueba nuestras vulnerabilidades: la invasión de Ceuta; ayer, Lituania y Dinamarca; hace pocos días, Alemania y Polonia. No son incidentes casuales: es una guerra híbrida declarada con forma de dron, de virus informático, de frontera e integridad territorial violada.

Quien ataque una frontera, quien invada un territorio europeo o quien noquee una infraestructura debe saber que Europa responderá inmediatamente, sin tener que esperar a un presidente como Sánchez, que se va de vacaciones en vez de defender nuestra frontera europea. El precio de no disuadir puede ser irreparable.

Necesitamos seguridad para ser libres y competitividad para ser autónomos, pero seguimos funcionando como 27 mercados pequeños. Necesitamos eliminar toda la burocracia, bajar los precios de la energía, invertir en digitalización; una industria made in Europe, nuevos acuerdos comerciales y completar el mercado único son el único camino para la Europa del futuro, un futuro que pasa, primero, por crear oportunidades y empleo para todos los jóvenes.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, «des mots, des mots, des mots», comme le disait Hamlet. Les mots comptent, mais pendant ce temps, en Europe, 500 travailleurs de l'industrie perdent leur travail chaque jour. Notre société est lacérée par ces usines qui ferment et notre souveraineté est minée. Voilà le coût de 30 années de religion du libre-échange. Le coût de l'humiliation heureuse face à Trump et le coût de la capitulation choisie face à la Chine. Nos batteries, nos terres rares, nos panneaux solaires, tout vient de Chine aujourd'hui. Nous dépendons totalement des plateformes et de l'intelligence artificielle américaines. Nos aéroports et nos chemins de fer sont visés par Poutine, et qu'annoncez-vous ce matin? Des panels, des débats stratégiques.

Il faut se réveiller. Nous voulons un plan européen d'investissement dans les industries de la transition écologique. Nous voulons enfin la préférence européenne, des marchés publics réservés aux productions européennes, la protection de nos usines contre le dumping chinois. Maintenant, nous voulons que vous appliquiez enfin les règles que nous avons votées contre les géants américains et chinois du numérique. Nous le voulons maintenant. Le temps n'est plus aux panels d'experts, le temps est aux actions. Alors agissons ensemble.

paragraphs.text: La guerre en Ukraine n'est pas simplement une guerre contre l'Ukraine: c'est une guerre contre l'ensemble du continent européen, c'est une guerre contre l'ensemble de nos nations. Et donc nous devons continuer à soutenir la résistance ukrainienne. Nous devons même faire beaucoup plus que ce que nous avons fait jusqu'ici; ce que nous devons faire désormais, c'est assumer la protection du ciel ukrainien contre les missiles russes qui visent les cibles civiles sur l'ensemble du territoire ukrainien.

Ce que des pays européens ont fait pour les Émirats arabes unis, pour le ciel d'Abu Dhabi, nous devons le faire aujourd'hui pour les villes ukrainiennes. Et donc, non, nous n'avons pas fait assez pour protéger l'Ukraine et nous n'avons pas fait assez pour défendre l'Europe. Ce qu'il nous faut, c'est l'autonomie stratégique européenne. Mais cela commence par quoi? Cela commence par augmenter notre soutien à la résistance ukrainienne.

paragraphs.text: Van der Leyen elnök asszony! Önök éveken át szemérmetlenül azt hazudták, hogy Magyarországon felszámolták a jogállamot. Pedig pontosan tudták, egy szó sem igaz az egészből. Azért csinálták ezt a kampányt, hogy visszatartsák az uniós forrásokat, és ezzel megbuktassák a patrióta magyar kormányt. Mai örömködése is ennek a beismerése.

Az elmúlt hónapokban aztán a TISZA-kormány alkotmányos puccsal felszámolta a demokratikus Magyarországot, és önkényuralmi rendszert hozott létre. Pontosan tudnak minderről, de most mégis hallgatnak. A fülsiketítő csendnek az az oka, hogy Brüsszel és a Tisza párt paktumot kötöttek. Magyar Péter dolga, hogy letörölje a nemzeti szuverenista erőket a magyar politika térképéről. Brüsszel pedig ezért az uniós pénzekkel és a feltétlen politikai támogatással fizet. A TISZA-kormány pedig a szuverenitásunkat teljesen feladva alávetett pozícióban beilleszti Magyarországot a brüsszeli birodalmi gépezetbe. De korán örülnek, mi harcolni fogunk az önkény ellen és a magyar szabadságért.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, faptul că Frau von der Leyen și-a cumpărat aplauzele nu schimbă realitatea, adică, supraîndatorarea UE și a statelor membre, dezindustrializarea și falimentul, sărăcia și șomajul populației. Cauzele? Vizibile, dar neluate în considerare: politicile infracționale din pandemie, măsurile iraționale din Green Deal și susținerea financiară obsesivă a regimului mafiot kievean.

UE este astăzi un liliputan economic care visează la inteligența artificială, dar s-a blocat în tehnologia dopului de plastic atașat pet-ului. Green Deal nu a adus energie sustenabilă, ci taxe și dependență de China.

Campioană la hiper-reglementare și promotoare a scutului democratic, adică a cenzurii, UE ne-a adus la un pas de război, în ciuda originilor pașnice ale UE. UE a devenit un pitic geopolitic indezirabil. State ca Islanda, Elveția și Norvegia își refuză accesul în UE, o organizație centralistă de tip sovietic.
Salvarea UE de la dezintegrare nu mai este acum posibilă decât dacă von der Leyen își dă demisia.

paragraphs.text: Fru formand! Tak, kære kolleger, president von der Leyen. Tak for en håbefuld tale. Jeg vil sige tre gange tak, og så vil jeg komme med et spørgsmål. Første tak er for at hædre den danske helikopterpilot Rune Kyndal. Jeg ved, at hans familie satte rigtig meget pris på det, der skete i dag, det var meget rørende.

Så en stor tak for at åbne over for Canada. Jeg er sikker på, at vi i morgen får en god tale fra Mr. Carney, og at der er blevet skrevet historie her i lokalet i dag. Det vil også være meget værdsat fra vores gruppes side for mig selv.

Og endelig en tak for at fokusere på goldplating. Vi har jo talt meget om goldplating. Jeg tror, vi har gjort alt, hvad vi kunne i Bruxelles efterhånden, nu mangler vi medlemsstaterne, jeg er helt enig. Og så skal vi altså være sikre på, at det rent faktisk sker, og mit spørgsmål til Dem, præsident, er derfor: Hvordan forestiller De Dem, at medlemsstaterne rent faktisk kan blive presset til at gøre det nødvendige, fordi det indtil nu har været et kæmpe problem. Jeg håber på at få en uddybning af det. Tak for det.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Prime Minister Carney, I'm really excited we are formalising our long-distance relationship. Of course, our history has had its ups and downs, but hey, we recently had a bad break-up with the Brits, and you seem to be going through a rough patch with the US. So, clearly, we are both open for something new.

For us, choosing you – Canada and Mr Carney – is quite easy. You have green hydrogen to keep us warm. You have maple syrup to keep us happy, and heated rivalry to keep us entertained. You have poutine, the Mounties, Celine Dion and Leonard Cohen, and of course, almost every famous Ryan or Justin I can think of.
Furthermore, you Canadians possess humankind's rarest skill, and that is the ability to apologise, which in today's ego-dominated world is very rare.
You have courage, Prime Minister, which you have shown by standing up against Trump's gaslighting – something we still have yet to learn.

We know that Canada will never be the 51st state, and apparently maybe also not the 28th Member State, even though you would be very welcome. But maybe we could become the 11th province of Canada, in addition to you being an associate member here.
Because we really need to double down – double double down – on our relationship. Long live Lake Ontario. Across the oceans our hearts will go on.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signora Presidente von der Leyen, nell'ultimo anno la Commissione ha presentato 41 iniziative sulla difesa e 31 sul sociale. Basta questo dato per spiegare la sua unica vera priorità: il riarmo.

L'Europa è spettatrice davanti all'avanzata dell'intelligenza artificiale, all'inflazione che sale, ai prezzi dell'energia e della benzina che sono alle stelle e sempre più cittadini non riescono ad arrivare a fine mese. La difesa deve essere anche protezione sociale e sicurezza del lavoro, che lei ignora.

Quando la politica smette di occuparsi della vita reale, la gente non smette di avere problemi: smette di credere nella politica ed è lì che cresce l'estrema destra. Non perché gli europei siano diventati estremisti ma perché qualcuno ha smesso di ascoltarli. E i problemi in Europa rimangono: la deindustrializzazione, la povertà, le disuguaglianze, la casa.

Presidente, più lei insegue la destra, più crescono i partiti neonazisti. Perché non tassiamo le Big Tech, gli extraprofitti, i miliardari per finanziare la giustizia sociale? Serve un'Europa più giusta, che lavori per la pace anziché boicottarla e difenda il lavoro e le nostre imprese e non insegua austerità e riarmo.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, tomei boa nota das suas palavras e trago números. Nos 90 segundos que tenho, a União Europeia gasta 1 milhão de EUR a importar energia, mais de 120 milhões nas três horas deste debate. Por isso, investir em energia limpa é investir na economia. É segurança, é competitividade, é liberdade.

Em 70 anos, aprendemos a circular sem fronteiras, e até já podemos pagar com a mesma moeda. Mas as empresas ainda enfrentam o rolo compressor de 27 leis nacionais, num mercado que devia ser único. Hoje, ainda não é possível criar uma empresa reconhecida em toda a Europa, e o mesmo vale para o Pacto das Migrações. Não podemos continuar com 27 políticas diferentes num espaço que se quer comum. E não podemos ceder a extremos. Portugal tem mostrado esse caminho. Só há política de migrações com regras. Só há dignidade se houver visto e contrato. Só há bem-estar se houver integração.

Os europeus não pedem que sonhemos por eles, pedem‑nos resultados, e há quem os espere com mais urgência do que nós. A Ucrânia não desistiu. Lembra‑nos todos os dias o que significa a Europa: um projeto de democracia, de paz e de liberdade. A presença do primeiro-ministro Mark Carney hoje mostra‑nos também uma verdade importante: as democracias não podem dar-se ao luxo de estar sozinhas, e a Europa é um espaço que vale a pena defender.

paragraphs.text: Fru talman! Ordförande von der Leyen. I Europa ser vi en växande backlash för jämställdheten, för flickors och kvinnors rättigheter. Jag välkomnar ert tal i dag, för det krävs vilja, mod och politiskt ledarskap för att ändra på attityder och strukturer. Jämställdheten måste integreras i alla politikområden, i lagstiftning, i budget. Varje euro vi använder och investerar ska bidra till ett jämställt Europa.

Lika viktigt är det att vi använder kvinnors kompetens. I dag står en tredjedel av alla Europas kvinnor utanför arbetsmarknaden. Inget jobb, ingen lön och ingen makt över sitt eget liv. Vi behöver kvinnors klokskap i den gröna omställningen, där det är avgörande att vi håller kursen för att klara 2040-målen.
Jag citerar gärna er, ordförande von der Leyen: "Women are here to stay". But we need results.
(Talaren avböjde två frågor (”blått kort”) från Jaak Madison och Cristian Terheş.)

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signora Presidente Von der Leyen, il suo è stato un monologo a senso unico, troppo scollato dalla realtà per quelle che sono le difficoltà che l'Europa sta vivendo.

Lei ha detto che abbiamo resistito, bene, a due guerre; ma probabilmente le sfugge quanto costano i carburanti, questa mattina, in quasi tutta Europa. Ha parlato di troppe regole, e io sono d'accordo, ma trovo poco credibile che quelli che l'hanno applaudita siano stati gli stessi che queste troppe regole hanno votato.

E poi lei ha parlato di un ruolo delle donne da difendere: io sono il primo ad essere d'accordo. Ma questa è una frase ipocrita, perché questa Commissione europea non ha mosso un dito contro la progressiva islamizzazione dell'Europa.

E, infine, lei riconosce che importiamo troppo dalla Cina. Ma Pechino non aveva bisogno di semafori verdi, quei semafori verdi che il Green Deal ha dato. Ma le assicuro una cosa: finché c'è la Lega, non permetteremo che l'Europa diventi una colonia cinese.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, collega’s, de woorden van deze Staat van de Unie worden hier altijd heel nauwgezet gewikt en gewogen, maar belangrijker zijn de acties die ondernomen worden op basis van prioriteiten. Er is één sleutel die de deur naar al die prioriteiten opent, en dat is economische groei.

Die groei is een absolute conditio sine qua non voor een krachtdadig beleid dat onze veiligheid, defensie en geopolitieke positie versterkt en onze bedrijven toelaat internationaal te concurreren. Daarvoor is echte deregulering nodig. Louter administratieve vereenvoudiging is onvoldoende. Europa moet meer ademruimte creëren voor creatief ondernemerschap. Minder regels en meer ruimte voor initiatief, investeringen en innovatie. En ook in de Europese begroting moet er dringend meer nadruk komen op onderzoek en ontwikkeling.
Zonder sterkere economische groei kunnen we zoveel ambities formuleren als we maar willen, maar we zullen ze zonder die economische groei niet kunnen realiseren.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, chapeau, Madam Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, I congratulate you for your condemnation of the horrifying scene from the state funeral of the convicted 'butcher from Srebrenica', Ratko Mladić.

The European Union needs enlargement to western Balkans as a strategic priority, but the message was sent and it is clear: the Union does not trade with its values. All victims and their families deserve truth and justice and compassion. This includes the truth about 1725 people still missing in Croatia following the Serbian aggression against Croatia. It also includes the missing Croats from Bugojno and eight Croatian children killed in Vitez in Bosnia and Herzegovina, for which, no one was held accountable.

The Irish minister mentioned the late John Hume, our former colleague who was instrumental in bringing peace to Northern Ireland. I hope that he will be remembered in this House by fully implementing the Dayton Peace Agreement and finally guaranteeing equal rights for all three constituent people in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And for that, we need the United States of America and keep working with our strongest transatlantic relations. And we also need strong trading partners and I welcome Canadian association membership. It is good to have Canada on board. It is good to have Canada that also our people have built and our diaspora, including my late uncle who is buried there.

Finally, I welcome your call for European firefighters fleet. But we must support the firefighters who carried out heroic work this summer in Croatia and across Europe, from Brač to Omiš, to all over. We need them in our sleepless night, they cannot fly, I mean, they are on the ground and we need to support them. We need to give them means to keep on fighting.

paragraphs.text: Pani poseł zwróciła uwagę na to, jak ważne są kwestie historyczne w polityce Unii Europejskiej, na podejście do praworządności i praw człowieka. Wróciłem nie tak dawno z Viannos w Grecji, gdzie grecki prezydent wspomniał, że do dzisiaj Grecja nie dostała reparacji wojennych od Niemiec. Do dzisiaj greccy obywatele nie mają żadnych roszczeń, żadnych świadczeń. Również mamy taką sytuację z Polską. Jak pani uważa: czy Komisja Europejska pod przewodnictwem pani von der Leyen powinna zmusić Niemcy, Berlin do podjęcia dialogu z Polską i Grecją? To jest stanowisko prezydentów Polski i Grecji, że taki dialog powinien się rozpocząć. Proszę odpowiedzieć na to pytanie.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, per rilanciare l'Europa ci vuole più pace e più giustizia: sette società digitali americane insieme valgono più del PIL dell'intera Unione. Non era mai accaduto nella storia dell'umanità.

È un modello sbilanciato. La ricchezza si continua a concentrare e non si distribuisce alle persone e il sistema fiscale globale è complice: le grandi piattaforme digitali pagano in media il 15% di imposte e i nostri commercianti, i nostri artigiani e le piccole e medie imprese ne pagano quasi il doppio. I giovani pagheranno una marea di tasse per ripagare i debiti. Questa è un'ingiustizia e combattere le ingiustizie è compito della democrazia. Ma la politica e i governi europei oggi non fanno niente.

Presidente, tocca all'Europa. Lei non ha detto nulla sulla tassa sui servizi digitali che ha annunciato nel 2020: è partita e poi fermata. Ecco, noi diciamo: paghino gli oligarchi e investiamo nell'innovazione, nella sanità, nella scuola, nella ricerca.
Perché non servono ora le parole. Serve che lei vada avanti per un insopprimibile, giusto senso di giustizia a cui occorre dare risposte, soprattutto per le ragazze e i ragazzi.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, mevrouw Von der Leyen, in welke realiteit leeft uw Commissie eigenlijk? U beweert veilige grenzen te garanderen. In werkelijkheid overspoelden nog maar enkele weken geleden 80 000 illegalen onze buitengrens in Ceuta. U beweert onze welvaart en concurrentiekracht te beschermen. In werkelijkheid is elektriciteit nu al 2,5 keer duurder en gas vijf keer duurder dan in de Verenigde Staten. En alsof dat nog niet genoeg is, legt u nog eens extra klimaattaksen op.
Uw plannen voor de toekomst? Een nieuwe Europese megabegroting van maar liefst 2 000 miljard euro. Nieuwe Europese belastingen. Meer van hetzelfde, maar dan gewoon duurder.

Waanzin is telkens opnieuw hetzelfde doen en toch een ander resultaat verwachten. Europa heeft een fundamenteel ander beleid nodig, dat van het gezond verstand. Want vroeg of laat, mevrouw, haalt de realiteit u in. En dan volgt de afrekening door de kiezer, en daar zullen wij voor zorgen.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Ursula von der Leyen has put this continent in danger.

Ms von der Leyen, your Green Deal is wrecking food security, businesses beg for relief, yet the regulatory monster you built keeps growing, even as you now try to scrap your own rules. You lost the race in AI and space. You close working power plants. You will kill combustion car factories in 2035. You celebrate 'achievements' while Europeans drown in living costs. Few have ruled Europe as long as you. For most of that time, Russia's illegal war has raged. And when illegal migrants arrive, you demand solidarity.

Green ideology has been your compass. With the EPP, you formed an unholy union with socialists. Equal misery – socialism – failed in Cuba, the Soviet Union and the European Union. Only a nationalist landslide can still save this continent.

paragraphs.text: Gospa predsednica, spoštovana predsednica Evropske komisije, dragi kolegi in kolegice, ko govorimo o prihodnosti Evrope, največkrat omenjamo konkurenčnost, gospodarsko rast, digitalizacijo, zeleni prehod in seveda našo varnost.
A prepogosto pozabljamo na temelj vsega, na demografijo. Demografija ni le vprašanje tega, koliko Evropejcev nas bo jutri, ampak tudi, kakšna bo Evropa jutri.
Ni zgolj statistika ali politika, je gospodarsko vprašanje, je socialno vprašanje in predvsem je ključni preizkus za našo prihodnost.

Pri tem imamo tudi v Evropskem parlamentu izjemno pomembno vlogo. Skupina za demografijo je ena najbolj aktivnih in angažiranih v tej hiši. To je seveda tudi dokaz, da lahko demografski izziv preseže politične delitve.

Evropska unija ima danes približno 450 milijonov prebivalcev. Napovedi so take, da nas bo čez nekaj let, desetletij, samo še štiristo. Hkrati se naše prebivalstvo stara. Do leta 2050 bo tako skoraj vsak tretji Evropejec starejši od 65 let.
To seveda pomeni manj delovno aktivnih ljudi, manjšo davčno osnovo in vse večji pritisk na naše pokojninske in zdravstvene sisteme.

To je realnost, s katero se moramo soočiti sedaj, ne jutri. Zato mora tudi demografija postati ena osrednjih politik in prioritet evropskega proračuna, ki je pred nami, ter stalni steber evropskih socialnih politik.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Frau Kommissionspräsidentin! Sie haben bereits letztes Jahr in Ihrer Rede auch erwähnt: Europa leidet unter einer massiven Wohnraumkrise. Immer mehr Menschen, vor allem junge Menschen, fragen sich: Kann ich mir mein Zuhause überhaupt noch leisten?

Wohnen ist eine der großen sozialen Fragen unserer Zeit geworden, und wir müssen endlich handeln − auch auf europäischer Ebene. Der Affordable Housing Act von Wohnkommissar Dan Jørgensen ist ein wichtiger erster Schritt in diese richtige Richtung. Aber es geht darum, nicht nur den Act umzusetzen, sondern auch weiterzudenken. Wir brauchen mehr Investitionen in leistbaren und sozialen Wohnraum und klare Regeln gegen Spekulationen.

Mein Appell an die Kommission ist auch: Leistbares Wohnen darf kein Nebenthema sein, sondern muss eine der großen Prioritäten der nächsten Jahre werden! Denn ein leistbares Zuhause ist keine Luxusfrage − es ist die Grundlage für ein gutes und selbstbestimmtes Leben überall in Europa.

Τσακίσατε τους αγρότες μας, τους κτηνοτρόφους και τους ψαράδες μας. Κλείνετε τα εργοστάσια της Ευρώπης και χάνονται εκατοντάδες χιλιάδες θέσεις εργασίας. Καταστρέψατε την πυρηνική οικογένεια. Μας επιβάλλετε τη «woke» ατζέντα, την πράσινη παράνοια, την ισλαμοποίηση της Ευρώπης. Πληρώνετε από την τσέπη μας τα εκατομμύρια λαθρομετανάστες που έχουν διαλύσει τις γειτονιές μας, βιάζουν, παρενοχλούν, δολοφονούν και, στο τέλος, τους δίνετε και χαρτιά για να ψηφίζουν. Αλλά μας δώσατε χάρτινα καλαμάκια, δεμένα καπάκια και gay pride. Δεν είστε απλά η καλύτερη μαθήτρια της Merkel. Την ξεπεράσατε, κυρία von der Leyen. Βουτηγμένη σε σκάνδαλα με βάσιμες υπόνοιες διαφθοράς, Pfizergate, εξαφανισμένα μηνύματα και άρνηση ελέγχου σας. Και όλα αυτά, χωρίς τη νομιμοποίηση της ψήφου των Ευρωπαίων πολιτών. Μόνο με τις πλάτες των σοσιαλιστών και του Weber. Κυρία von der Leyen, μας ρημάξατε.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Frau Kommissionspräsidentin! Herr Ratsvertreter! Liebe Kolleginnen, liebe Kollegen! Das Angebot einer assoziierten Partnerschaft mit Kanada, das ja weit über ein Freihandelsabkommen hinausgeht, ist ein ganz klares, starkes Bekenntnis, das ich sehr begrüße. Es zeigt nämlich, dass wir Europäer verlässliche Partner in der Welt sind und dass auch wir in der Welt verlässliche Partner haben, die unsere Werte teilen. Ich begrüße das ausdrücklich und hoffe sehr, dass das eine ganz, ganz strenge Partnerschaft, eine schöne Gemeinschaft werden wird.

Frau Präsidentin, Sie haben eine gute Rede gehalten. Ich danke Ihnen für Ihre realistischen Standortbestimmungen und auch für die vielen richtigen Themen, die Sie angesprochen haben: unsere Sicherheit, unsere Wettbewerbsfähigkeit hier in der Europäischen Union, Vorschläge zum Umgang mit künstlicher Intelligenz und sozialen Medien. Ich finde, das ist alles richtig und wichtig.

Entscheidend ist aber, dass wir diesen Ankündigungen jetzt auch Taten folgen lassen, denn unsere Bürger fragen sich: Was macht ihr eigentlich für uns? Ich begrüße Ihren Vorschlag eines Kids Acts, denn der Schutz unserer Kinder im Netz ist zentral. Und ich begrüße auch, dass Sie das Thema Wettbewerbsfähigkeit zu Ihrer Toppriorität gemacht haben. Tausende Jobs gehen tagtäglich in unseren europäischen Ländern verloren. Die Menschen haben Angst, sind verunsichert.

Deshalb müssen wir alles unternehmen, um unsere Wirtschaft zu entlasten und für faire Wettbewerbsbedingungen zu sorgen. Ich sage auch: Ja, es ist richtig, gold-plating anzugehen und die Mitgliedstaaten zu fordern, aber auch die Kommission darf in ihren Bemühungen um Bürokratieabbau ...

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, também nós queremos construir uma União Europeia próspera, mas isso não acontecerá se esquecermos a proteção do ambiente e da saúde. E desde o início deste mandato que assistimos ao desmantelar do Pacto Ecológico Europeu. O regulamento antidesflorestação, a lei relativa à monitorização das florestas europeias, o Fundo Social para o Clima — todos os compromissos traídos. As ondas de calor deste verão e os incêndios florestais mostraram bem o desafio que enfrentamos e só são uma novidade para os distraídos.

Mas, como disse, Senhora Presidente, quando a Europa está dividida, não consegue mudar o rumo dos acontecimentos. Queremos também que não se esqueça, por favor, do compromisso com a União Europeia da Saúde, que é muito mais do que inteligência artificial ou competitividade industrial. Muitos europeus continuam a adoecer e a morrer por causas evitáveis. Tabaco, álcool, poluição, gorduras saturadas e trans... Precisamos de uma agenda para a prevenção. E sim, Presidente, para tudo isto precisamos de mais recursos comuns. E as receitas do sistema de crédito de emissões e do tabaco aqui, sim, podem dar uma ajuda.

paragraphs.text: First of all, you said that in the last few years Ms von der Leyen has changed course about the Green Deal. I have to remind you that two years ago we had elections, and the voters said in Europe clearly that they would like to see a more realistic approach to the climate ideology, because that is why the conservatives just said a lot of things to the socialists.

But, just realistically, if we go along with the Green Deal and so on to adapt to climate change and so on, just what is your approach? Currently we are importing about 80 % of the minerals from China and from Africa controlled by Chinese. How are we going to guarantee that everybody will have electricity without fossil fuels all over the Europe? How are you going to guarantee that?

paragraphs.text: Em primeiro lugar, eu não disse que a senhora presidente tinha desistido do Pacto Ecológico Europeu; eu disse que alguns nesta casa tinham desistido do Pacto Ecológico Europeu. É bom que isso fique claro.

Em segundo lugar, é bom que também recordem aos europeus que eles não enchem o tanque dos seus carros com aquilo que não é pagável por eles próprios. E isso tem a ver com a descarbonização, um roteiro verde e eletrificação da Europa, não com aquilo que os senhores acham que tem a ver.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedkyně, paní předsedkyně Komise, musím říct, že jsem měla připravený jiný projev, ale váš projev mě tak říkajíc zvedl ze židle. Více než 30 let sloužím veřejnosti. Jsem v politických funkcích, ale to, co jsem dneska zažila, je pro mě něco nepřijatelného. Možná vás teď překvapím. Já také věřím v Evropu, ale v úplně jinou než vy. Silná Evropa totiž není více nařízení, regulací, omezení. Silná Evropa je diskuse. Silná Evropa je pluralita názorů. Silná Evropa je hledání kompromisů. Silná Evropa je 27 silných států. Silná Evropa je respekt k druhým, k jejich specifikům. Silná Evropa je akceptace výsledků voleb. Silná Evropa není propaganda, není nálepkování, není jediný správný názor a není vytváření cordon sanitaire. Silná Evropa není silná Evropská komise. Evropská komise není evropská vláda a vy nejste její prezidentkou. Naštěstí.
(Řečnice odmítl tři otázky, které chtěli zvednutím modré karty položit Diana Iovanovici Şoşoacă, Ondřej Dostál a Tomáš Zdechovský.)

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, el 4 de agosto apareció un dron cargado de explosivos en el aeropuerto de Leipzig. Ayer, desde el círculo más íntimo de Putin, se advirtió a Polonia de que dejaría de existir en dos o tres días. Y a finales de julio, en dos noches, más de 80 000 personas cruzaron la frontera de Ceuta. 80 000 personas no fuerzan una frontera si no lo permite el país del que salen. Tres hechos, tres geografías, un solo método.
Los ataques híbridos no distinguen entre el Báltico y el estrecho de Gibraltar. Buscan nuestra grieta y confían en que tratemos esa grieta como un problema local.

Señora presidenta, Ceuta es hoy el «estado de la Unión Europea». Es una ciudad que está sosteniendo sola lo que debería sostener un continente. Más de 10 000 personas deambulan por sus calles sin que Marruecos las acepte de vuelta.

España no es menos parte de la Unión Europea que Alemania o Polonia. La amenaza híbrida por el sur no es menos grave y quienes nos atacan de forma híbrida por el sur no deberían merecer menos sanciones que aquellos que lo hacen por el este. La grieta que buscan quienes nos provocan no está en la valla de Ceuta, está en esta Cámara y estará en esta Cámara el día que consideremos Leipzig un problema alemán, Varsovia un problema polaco o Ceuta un problema español.
Señora presidenta, le felicito por su discurso. Gracias por su estrategia contra la guerra híbrida. Pero, por favor, el flanco sur es de la misma magnitud que el flanco este.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Debatujemy dzisiaj o tym, w jakim stanie jest Unia Europejska. Dobrze to ilustruje sytuacja sprzed kilku tygodni w hiszpańskiej Ceucie. 70 tysięcy osób szturmowało granicę maleńkiej Ceuty. Po 48 godzinach działania służb opanowano kryzys. Prawie wszyscy przebywający na terenie Ceuty wrócili do Maroka. Ale oczywiście ekstremistyczna prawica postanowiła wykorzystać ten akt wojny hybrydowej. Ponadto, niestety, wielu przywódców państw Unii Europejskiej napisało list także do pani, pani przewodnicząca. Czy zaoferowali w nim pomoc Hiszpanii? Nie, wykorzystano kryzys, w którym zginęło 140 osób, by skrytykować odnoszący sukcesy kraj rządzony przez lewicę.

Kiedy kilka lat temu Polska, mój kraj, zmagała się z kryzysem na granicy białoruskiej, organizowanym przez dyktaturę Łukaszenki, Europa zaproponowała ludzi, sprzęt i pieniądze. I to była pomoc, której potrzebuje dzisiaj Hiszpania. Czy reakcja na Ceutę to był przypadek tej słynnej europejskiej solidarności, czy raczej podwójnych standardów? Nie pokonamy nacjonalistów, udając nacjonalistów. Pokonamy autokratów solidarnością europejską.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, doamnă președintă von der Leyen, realitățile prezentate de dumneavoastră astăzi aici nu pot fi contestate. Le simțim și noi, și cetățenii pe care îi reprezentăm. Vorbim despre securitate și competitivitate, despre o Europă puternică.
Pentru România și statele estice, amenințările la adresa securității nu sunt abstracte. Vedem dronele rusești în fiecare zi.
Dar securitatea Europei înseamnă și securitatea alimentară. Ieri, fermierii din România au ieșit în stradă, și mă uit la domnul Várhelyi, de la care aștept un licăr de speranță pentru ei.

Vocea lor însă este vocea fermierilor europeni. Aceștia doresc să aibă șansa de a-și continua munca. După o vară fierbinte, marcată de secetă și inundații, de criza îngrășămintelor și a combustibililor, fermierii se luptă cu dușmani cu care nu-și pot măsura singuri puterile, și de aceea noi trebuie să fim lângă ei.

Jean Monnet spunea că „Europa va fi făurită în criză și va fi suma soluțiilor adoptate pentru depășirea acestor crize”. Astăzi, fermierii Europei au nevoie ca noi să fim la înălțimea acestor cuvinte. Când avem grijă de agricultura Europei, avem grijă de viitor.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Sehr geehrte Frau Kommissionspräsidentin! Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Die europäische Erfolgsformel ist ziemlich einfach. Sie lautet: Binnenmarkt, Binnenmarkt, Binnenmarkt. Und was unser Binnenmarkt braucht, sind Investitionen und Einheitsrecht. Es braucht Freiheit, und es braucht den Schutz auf europäischer Ebene.

Frau von der Leyen, die Omnibusse sind gescheitert. Sie sind Stückwerk und lösen das Problem nicht einheitlich. Sie bauen Schutzstandards ab und schwächen unsere Rolle als globaler Standardsetter. Wir brauchen keine Deregulierung! Die Omnibusse haben Ihre Mehrheit in diesem Haus gespalten.

Was wir eigentlich brauchen, ist mehr Einheitsrecht. Wir müssen etwas zusammen aufbauen, so wie wir es bei EU Inc. tun – aber nicht, wie es die Kommission vorgeschlagen hat, sondern wir brauchen eine EU Inc., bei der es mehr Freiheit für Gründerinnen und Gründer gibt und der Schutz der Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer auf derselben Ebene gleichrangig geregelt wird. paragraphs.text: Szanowna Pani Przewodnicząca! Szanowna Pani Komisarz! Z dumą dzisiaj mówię po polsku, bo przywołane przez panią komisarz polskie przykłady dają poczucie dumy i satysfakcji.

Chciałoby się poprosić o więcej polskich pomysłów realizowanych na rzecz silnej, wspólnej Europy: Rafał Modrzewski i jego innowacyjna firma budująca bezpieczeństwo, ochrona granicy polsko-białoruskiej, tak skutecznej, że dzisiaj nie ma jednego nielegalnego migranta, nie tylko fizyczna ochrona, ale także prawna, zawieszenie prawa do azylu. To przykłady, że przy solidarności europejskiej i zrozumieniu możemy działać skutecznie także w przypadku Ceuty, bo wszyscy dzisiaj jesteśmy mieszkancami Ceuty. Chcemy bezpiecznej Ceuty. Chcemy granicy europejskiej, sprawnie chronionej, skutecznie chronionej.

Ale dzisiaj najważniejszym wyzwaniem jest bezpieczeństwo. Tak, realne zagrożenie istnieje na naszych granicach i lotniskach. To już nie jest hybrydowe zagrożenie, to jest realne zagrożenie. Dlatego musimy budować koalicję siły i determinacji, by Europa była silna, sprawna, ale też bezpieczna. To jest oczekiwanie naszych obywateli.

I mam apel do was wszystkich na tej sali, bo kończymy tę debatę. Ta konkluzja powinna być jedna i wspólna, ponad podziałami politycznymi, na rzecz wspólnej Europy, bo ona jest atrakcyjna także dla takich partnerów jak Kanada, partnerów pozaeuropejskich. To najważniejszy projekt polityczny, by zapewnić sobie bezpieczeństwo ponad podziałami politycznymi. Budujmy koalicję siły. A przyjaciele Putina, którzy tu siedzą i chcą nas podzielić, niech zostaną w koalicji strachu. Patrioci, którzy czasem ignorują to zagrożenie: dołączcie do koalicji siły, jeżeli chcecie być patriotami, a nie zdrajcami.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, citizens want to feel safe, they want good jobs and better opportunities, and they want Europe to deliver. But some politicians want Europe to achieve more with less. It will not work. You cannot ask Europe to compete to protect its borders and strengthen its security while cutting the EU budget.

And we cannot build a stronger Europe by leaving regions behind. Cohesion is at the heart of the European project. Social Europe is the definition of what we stand for. Children's future should not depend on the postcode where they are born. This is why the next EU long-term budget is a defining choice. Europe has to invest more in creating better jobs, health and education. We need to invest in people first. This is what Europeans, this is what Romanians expect.
We must also recognise the specific challenges faced by eastern countries, which require urgent solutions. If we want Europe to deliver, we must give Europe the means to act.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, bene il Kids Act: la risposta deve essere europea. La responsabilità è delle piattaforme: non è dei minori e delle famiglie. Non discutiamo più soltanto di ciò che i ragazzi fanno con i social, ma di ciò che i social fanno ai ragazzi.

E abbiamo ascoltato da lei una proposta concreta: niente social sotto i 13 anni, accesso supervisionato fino ai 15 e, soprattutto, un limite di 1 ora al giorno. Una scelta forte e necessaria. Poi maggiore autonomia, sempre su piattaforme sicure.

E concludo ricordando le sue parole sulla disinformazione e le fake news: abbiamo bisogno della sovranità digitale europea e di algoritmi trasparenti per battere le fake news. Proteggere il nostro spazio digitale significa proteggere la nostra democrazia e la libertà di ciascuno di formarsi un'opinione senza manipolazioni.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Megszoktuk már, hogy amikor Ursula von der Leyen Bizottsága nem teljesít egy korábban meghirdetett programot, akkor ezt tucatnyi új programmal próbálja elfedni. A mai beszédében több mint negyven új stratégiát, programot és intézményt jelentett be. Csak a lényegről nem akarnak beszélni. Arról, hogy a korábbi döntéseikkel az egekbe tolták az energiaárakat. A Draghi-jelentés leírta, hogy az európai vállalatok négy-ötszörös árat fizetnek az energiáért a versenytársaikhoz képest, és ennek ellenére a Bizottság nem bővítette, hanem szűkítette egyes tagállamok beszerzési lehetőségeit, többek között tiltásokkal.

A következmények itt vannak. Az európai ipar lejtmenetben van, csak a Volkswagen 50 ezer dolgozót rúg majd ki, de egyes helyeken 100 ezerről írnak. És ezek után még azt mondja az Európai Bizottság elnöke, hogy Európa jobban kezelte a válságot, mint gondolta volna. Hát hol él, Elnök Asszony? Járt mostanában benzinkútnál? Amit látunk, az az európai állam elárulása. AI-gyanús, üres szólamok...

Την ίδια ώρα που κάνετε αυτή τη δήλωση, όμως, στην Κύπρο τουρκικά drones και μαχητικά τουρκικά αεροσκάφη παρενοχλούν πτήσεις πολιτικών αεροσκαφών στα αεροδρόμια Λάρνακας και Πάφου. Χρησιμοποιούν τα κατεχόμενα εδάφη της Κύπρου για να παρενοχλούν επιβατικά αεροσκάφη —επαναλαμβάνω: επιβατικά αεροσκάφη—, με ένα από αυτά να αναγκάζεται να παρεκκλίνει από την πορεία του για να μη συγκρουστεί στον αέρα, θέτοντας σε κίνδυνο χιλιάδες ζωές αθώων ανθρώπων.

Θα συνεχίσετε να παρακολουθείτε αμέτοχοι τις προκλήσεις, αποκαλώντας την Τουρκία ως εταίρο ή θα περάσετε από τα λόγια στις πράξεις; Κουραστήκαμε με την υποκρισία. Φτάνουν τα δύο μέτρα και τα δύο σταθμά. Η Ευρώπη οφείλει να υπερασπίζεται στην πράξη κάθε κράτος μέλος της...

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Sie haben gesagt: „Es geht um Taten, nicht Worte.“ Vor einem Jahr habe ich gesagt: „Österreich-Zuschlag − wir zahlen mehr für Produkte als in Deutschland.“ Das verstößt gegen den Binnenmarkt. Bitte, wann tun Sie endlich etwas?

Zweiter Punkt: Democracy Shield − haben Sie angesprochen. Wir haben einen großartigen Ausschuss gehabt. Jetzt geht es um die Umsetzung dieses Resilience Centre. Ich erwarte, dass da dieses Parlament, dieser Ausschuss, eingebunden werden. Bitte sorgen Sie dafür.

Drittens: Außenpolitik − wir haben die Hohe Vertreterin für Außen- und Sicherheitspolitik. Was tun Sie dafür, dass sie eine gemeinsame europäische Außenpolitik umsetzen kann, die wir ja dringend brauchen, was Sie auch gesagt haben? Bitte, wenn Sie dazu auch etwas sagen können.

Und dann möchte ich zum Schluss noch sagen, ein österreichischer Rechtsextremer hat zuerst gesagt, die EU sei in den dunkelsten Stunden ihrer Geschichte. Das hat mich sehr gekränkt, als Österreicher mit unserer Geschichte. Bitte, es muss Ihnen klar sein, mit diesen Rechtsextremen können Sie kein Europa aufbauen ...

interventions.speaker_label: Ursula von der Leyen, President of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, thank you very much for this very lively debate and your endurance.
Let me respond to some of the topics. Of course, I will not be able to cover all if I want to stay within the limits of the time and not go overdue like I did this morning.

To Morten Løkkegaard, you asked me how to engage the Council to deliver faster. I think what we have to do is put the spotlight on – have a public debate. For example, the EU Inc. proposal is a very good example of how we can put more pressure and speed on it.

As you might recall, at the moment, people who want to set up a company in the European Union have to deal with 27 different legal systems and 60 different forms of company. This is why we have proposed EU Inc. – one single and simple rule for the whole of the European Union. You can set up your company within 48 hours totally online, for less than EUR 100.

The IMF estimates that the 28th regime could increase our GDP by more than 3 % over ten years, and the business sector is waiting for it. One hundred tech founders and investors told us just last week to get EU Inc. right.

Therefore, I'm calling on you, because we have to be very careful – and that's putting the spotlight on it – within the legislative process – and I'm not speaking here of the Parliament – that we are not turning this very straightforward regulation into one with 27 different national variations like we have with a directive. We have to be very careful that we do not turn this speedboat that is so necessary into a heavy tanker that would disappoint everyone. So, please let's get EU Inc. done and let it get done right.
(Applause)

My second point is about investment. I heard many, many priorities – and you are absolutely right – from social to competitiveness, from farmers to nature, from jobs to infrastructure, and many, many more priorities.

The answer to that lies in a strong European budget. I am preaching here in the wrong church. I know it. But I have to say it again: we have to get the budgetary equation right. The budgetary equation is: if we want to keep national contributions stable, if we want to invest in our priorities, and if we want to pay back Next Generation EU, we need new own resources. I know you are allies in that, but I want to emphasise this once again very clearly.

Then I've heard critics about the summer and how to fight the heatwave impact. I want to stand up here for the European response. The Emergency Response Coordination Centre, abbreviation ERCC, oversaw the deployment of 40 aircraft, 18 ground teams. Almost 800 firefighters have been positioned in advance in 14 different European countries. The colleagues worked day and night, and indeed, we have to thank them here from the bottom of our hearts for this outstanding work.
(Applause)

I'll use my last minute for one topic that is close to my heart. Today, honourable Members, we mark the anniversary of Daphne Galizia's murder. Exactly five years ago, I had the honour of visiting her memorial with her family. I remember their hope that justice would soon be made. Today, it is disheartening to see that the pursuit of justice is not over yet.

Yes, Daphne's legacy has inspired our Media Freedom Act. We passed legislation to protect journalists, because they must be free to do their job safely. We remain vigilant on this case and on media freedom across the Union with our rule of law reports.
Let me be clear. Daphne devoted her entire life to seeking the truth, and now truth must prevail. There can be no impunity for Daphne's murder.
(Applause)
I will use my last 15 seconds to say I leave this debate encouraged. I heard critics – yes, that's democracy – but much more strong support.
So, here, for the pro-Europeans: let's stand together, let's work together, let's make a strong and independent Europe together.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Frau von der Leyen, leider bleiben Sie sozialpolitisch ein Totalausfall. Bezahlbare Energie für Haushalte an der Tanke, bezahlbare Lebensmittel, bezahlbare Miete – das kommt bei Ihnen gar nicht vor. Die Sicherung von Industriearbeitsplätzen – bei Ihnen nur eine Randbemerkung. Übergewinnsteuern für Energiemultis, für Rüstungsunternehmen oder eine Digitalsteuer für Big-Tech-Unternehmen – bei Ihnen Fehlanzeige.

Stattdessen versprechen Sie Geschenke an Rüstungsunternehmen; die Bilanzen der Banken sollen vergoldet werden. Diese Politik richtet sich gegen den sozialen Zusammenhalt in Europa und ist ein reines Jobvernichtungsprogramm. Ihre Politik hilft nicht den arbeitenden Menschen, aber sie stärkt die extreme Rechte in diesem Haus. Deshalb, Frau von der Leyen, zeigt diese Debatte, dass wir keine weiteren Debatten über die Zukunft der Europäischen Union in diesem Format brauchen, sondern dass es eine bezahlbare Zukunft für die Menschen in der Europäischen Union braucht.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, today I have criticised the Commission President and her plans, and I will continue to do so, as I would with any politician from the democratic spectrum. But after this debate, I must very clearly say that the far right do not – either in this House or anywhere else in Europe – give any answers to the challenges that are ahead of us. None. Zero. All I heard today were racist, anti-European, spiteful statements attacking the President and the European Union, with colleagues defending the likes of Trump and Putin in this world. With these people, no problems in Europe will be solved.

So while we are clear about our differences, a Europe of the future will only be built if pro-Europeans are working together. So let us fight. And let us discuss the best ideas, but also let us work together to deliver for the citizens of Europe. It is high time we act.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, serve unità per l'autonomia strategica europea, un'alleanza forte delle forze europeiste per dare quelle risposte chiare ai cittadini e alle cittadine europee, che vivono un momento di enorme difficoltà.

Il costo dell'energia, della benzina, alloggi, cibo hanno toccato livelli insostenibili: solo il costo del cibo, negli ultimi cinque anni, è aumentato del 30%, e chi, invece, quel cibo lo produce non vede un centesimo di questo aumento.

Alcuni strumenti ci sono: bisogna lavorarci di più. Penso alle filiere corte, a produttori più forti, a norme contro le pratiche commerciali sleali, a diritti dei lavoratori e a una minore dipendenza da energia e fertilizzanti importati. Un cibo equo, sano, la difesa del pianeta e il Green Deal, il reddito degli agricoltori devono stare nella stessa politica europea.

La credibilità degli impegni che si è assunta oggi, Presidente von der Leyen, si misurerà sulle azioni concrete che farà la sua Commissione e sulla coerenza dei gruppi che in quest'Aula dicono di sostenere un'Europa forte.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Commission President, you started by quoting Dickens: 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.' That somehow aptly described also the debate that followed. I am an optimist, and I believe, when we are speaking about the future of Europe, that there is so much that binds us, and the agenda you presented today should be embraced by a pro-European majority, because giving hope and confidence to citizens also starts from this House. We cannot inspire citizens, if we ourselves cannot move beyond blame games. And there is so much we can do together. And I liked Valérie Hayer's idea of pro-European radicalism. The EPP will take care of the pro-European. I am sure others can provide the radicalism.

Colleagues, the state of the Union is the state we decide to build, and the EPP has a vision of a strong, competitive and safe Europe, and we have a record of delivering on it. And this is what we will continue to do.

paragraphs.text: Laura Ballarín Cereza (S&D), por escritoDurante el debate del Estado de la Unión, nuestro Grupo ha pedido a la presidenta de la Comisión, valentía en la defensa de la Europa que hemos construido frente a una retorno del nacionalismo, para afrontar el cambio climático y alcanzar la neutralidad climática para 2050, garantizar la competitividad con energía limpia, segura y asequible. Hemos pedido acelerar las renovables e imponer un impuesto sobre los beneficios extraordinarios de las empresas energéticas para financiar un esquema de apoyo social a las familias.Hemos pedido: una Ley Europea de Vivienda y actuar sobre los alquileres de corta duración; una ley de empleos de calidad con reglas justas para la inteligencia artificial en el trabajo; defender nuestras fronteras sin abandonar nuestros valores; y defender la paz y el derecho internacional: suspender el acuerdo con Israel, imponer sanciones y un embargo de armas.Hay que poner los activos rusos congelados al servicio de la reconstrucción de Ucrania Necesitamos un presupuesto a la altura, sin recortes en la política de cohesión agrícola o en inversión social.Hemos pedido también protección explicita de los derechos de las mujeres, tipificar y blindar el delito de feminicidio y defender el derecho al aborto.

paragraphs.text: Romana Jerković (S&D), in writingMadam President,Five years ago, during COVID, I heard your strong words and bold ambitions about building a European Health Union. But since then, you seem to have lost sight of what the European Health Union actually is, and what it takes to build it.The European Health Union is not a finished project. It is an evolving one, which must adapt and grow as new health challenges emerge.And indeed, the challenges are already here.Healthcare workforce shortages. Unequal access to treatment. Environmental health threats. The rise of non-communicable diseases. And the growing use of artificial intelligence, with all the opportunities and ethical questions it brings.Madam President, these challenges demand European attention. Health cannot disappear from our political priorities simply because the pandemic has.We started building a European Health Union in a crisis. Now we must have the political will to continue building it beyond one.

paragraphs.text: Kinga Kollár (PPE), in writingEuropeans want Europe to be much stronger. This is a practical necessity in an increasingly competitive and uncertain world.Being stronger means more strategic thinking and a faster capacity to act. Less bureaucracy, fewer excuses, and less useless political manipulation.Europe cannot afford to spend years discussing challenges while others are already acting and harm is underway. How do we treat China? How do we achieve a true single market? How artificial intelligence will impact our way of life?There are no easy answers to these questions, but diverse opinions and interests should not paralyze brave and clear decision-making.Secondly, the actions we take must be much swifter — our own rules cannot result in legislation being adopted years after the need for it arises. It is time for Europe to move forward with greater ambition and much faster implementation. We need to focus on delivering for our citizens and not on ideological differences. Those who only make noise or manipulate based on human fears, do not contribute to real progress.Colleagues, we all need to live up to our responsibility and progress faster on key challenges. This is why people elected us; this is what we need to do.

To wazny krok na drodze do integracji.

Ta współpraca oparta na demokracji, praworządności i wolnym rynku zyskuje zupełnie nowy wymiar. By budować silniejsze gospodarki i bardziej odporne społeczeństwa. To wazny krok na drodze do integracji.

paragraphs.text: Dan-Ştefan Motreanu (PPE), în scrisObservăm tot mai clar, în alegerile din regiunile mai slab dezvoltate ale Uniunii Europene, cum costul ridicat al vieții, inflația, lipsa investițiilor, a competitivității și a locurilor de muncă bine plătite duc la pierderea încrederii în partidele de centru și la o creștere îngrijorătoare a extremelor. Avem nevoie de o politică inteligentă și bine finanțată pentru dezvoltarea și modernizarea acestor regiuni, cu atât mai mult cu cât negociem acum viitorul buget al Uniunii Europene pentru perioada 2028–2034, într-un context în care unele state membre susțin în Consiliu reduceri semnificative ale anvelopei bugetare propuse. Avem nevoie nu doar de consolidarea fondurilor de coeziune și a Pilonului II al Politicii Agricole Comune, ci și de sinergii reale cu Fondul European pentru Competitivitate, pentru ca regiunile mai slab dezvoltate să poată participa la lanțurile valorice europene, să ofere oportunități antreprenorilor și IMM-urilor și să atragă investiții industriale majore, evitând astfel riscul unei Uniuni mai competitive în ansamblu, dar mult mai fragmentate în interior, cu consecințe asupra opțiunilor politice ale cetățenilor.

paragraphs.text: Matjaž Nemec (S&D), pisnoSpoštovane in spoštovani!Evropa mora stati za Evropejci. To so velika načela, ki jih zlahka izgovorimo, a suverenosti ne gradijo lepe besede v Strasbourgu, temveč odločna dejanja!Gledamo svet vojn, trgovinskih spopadov in tehnoloških groženj. Pozdravljamo regulacijo umetne inteligence, zeleni prehod ter obrambo pravic žensk. A kaj pomagajo analize, če tretjina obljub Komisije ostaja neuresničena? Kaj pomagajo obljube o suverenosti, ko pa se največji evropski dosežek - schengen - pred našimi očmi izginja in ostaja zgolj še črka na papirju?Najbolj pa bode v oči dvoličnost. Medtem ko se v Gazi nadaljuje genocid in gledamo kršitve mednarodna prava s strani Izraela, se Evropa skriva za neenotnostjo in ponuja zgolj prazne besede namesto konkretnih sankcij. To ni voditeljstvo, to je izmikanje odgovornosti. Zadnjo skupno izjavo glede širitve nezakonitih naselbin v območju E1 je blokirala Slovenija, ki postaja zgolj vazal za izvajanje interesov Izraela v Evropi. Puščico je von der Leyen usmerila v svoji kritiki tudi v aktualno slovensko vlado. Ljudje ne potrebujejo priročnikov za prihodnost, potrebujejo rezultate danes! V S&D ne bomo tiho gledali neukrepanja. Bojevali se bomo za socialno, pravično in solidarno Evropo, kjer mednarodno pravo velja za vse, brez izjem in brez dvojnih meril. Časa za odlašanje je zmanjkalo!

paragraphs.text: Mirosława Nykiel (PPE), na piśmieBardzo dziękuje za Pani odpowiedzialną wizję Europy a szczególnie za potrzebę budowania odporności demokracji. Absolutnie się z tym zgadzam. Ataki Rosji to nie tylko czołgi i rakiety nie tylko czołgi i rakiety to także propaganda, dezinformacja i próba podważenia wiary Europejczyków w demokrację i wolność.I musimy powiedzieć jasno: nie możemy pozwolić, aby kolejne pokolenie zapomniało, dlaczego powstała Unia Europejska.Dlatego proponuję europejski program „From Generation to Generation” — program, który w sposób systemowy będzie uczył w naszych szkołach o demokracji, wolności, prawach człowieka, solidarności i historii europejskiej integracji.Bo jeśli chcemy obronić Europę jutra, musimy zacząć od edukacji dzieci Europy dzisiaj i niezależnie od wysiłku i starań krajów członkowskich musimy podjąć działania europejskie. Mam konkretną propozycję takiego projektu. Przedstawiłam już ten projekt Przewodniczącej Parlamentu Europejskiego i uzyskał on jej poparcie. Wierzę, że razem możemy go zrealizować.Czy możemy liczyć na poparcie i zaangażowanie Komisji Europejskiej, aby wspólnie stworzyć program „From Generation to Generation”

paragraphs.text: Ивайло Вълчев (ECR), в писмена формаЧухме от г-жа фон дер Лайен много неща, които, ние, дясно мислещите консервативни хора сме повтаряли с години. Защитата на границата, спирането на нелегалната миграция, укрепването на Европа като геополитически фактор, стимулиране на икономиката чрез намаляване на бюрократичната тежест и насърчаване на иновации и инвестиции. Това, което обаче не чухме е кога ще се случи и как. Европейска комисия и в преднишния, и в настоящия мандат продължава вредните за Европа политики. Например, сега чухме за намерението да се създаде „Конгрес на Европа“, което силно противоречи на идеята за намаляването на бюрокрацията.Всъщност, години наред слушаме за по-доброто бъдеще, по-ниските цени на енергията, за това как „Зелената сделка“ ни прави по-богати. Резултатът обаче е точно обратният. Поне в моите очи. Както чухме от председателя на ЕК, Съюзът е в най-добрата си кондиция. Нищо, че губим икономическата надпревара от САЩ и Китай, нищо, че не сме фактор при взимането на решения дори за войната, която е на границата ни- в Украйна, нищо, че индустрията се изнася извън Европа, заради регулации и високи цени на енергията.Европейският съюз трябва отново да се превърне в място, където си струва да произвеждаш, инвестираш и създаваш работни места.По-малко бюрокрация. По-достъпна енергия. Повече свобода за бизнеса.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, we have the thing called the single market. It's our holy grail. But we live in uncertain times where the competition is getting tougher. We just voted for the Customs Authority, and the funding for it is in this mandate.

But that's not all. We need to do much, much more. We need to work with fair competition, anti-fraud, and tax cooperation. We need to do this because a lot has changed during these years. We have new geopolitical challenges, we have new ways of trade, and we have a record flow of goods from all around the world.

We need to do this because the single market is so important for us. We need to protect it from unfair competition. While doing that, we protect our workers, our businesses and our jobs – which is the most important thing we can do.
Basically, what we try to do with this mandate is to make sure to close the gaps in the fence, but still keep a door open for our friends. We need to be fair, but not naive, to all of them around us.
I really hope to get good support for this, so we can take this forward in a good manner and have a better result after the negotiations.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, GOVSATCOM e Iris rappresentano una risposta europea alla necessità di garantire comunicazioni affidabili in un contesto caratterizzato da lacune di connettività e minacce informatiche.

Su questi due voti: da un lato, l'Unione mantiene proprietà esclusiva degli asset connessi a quelle che sono le infrastrutture sviluppate, mentre l'Islanda e la Norvegia rappresentano due partner affidabili dello Spazio economico europeo.
In conclusione, sotto il profilo finanziario non ci sono oneri di bilancio ma, al contrario, entrate con destinazione specifica. Per questo chiedo il supporto dell'Aula.

paragraphs.text: Gerbiamas pirmininke, gerbiami kolegos. Ignalinos atominės elektrinės uždarymas yra ne vien Lietuvos, bet tai yra visos Europos atsakomybė, nes prieš daugiau nei dvidešimt metų, kai Lietuva priėmė labai sudėtingą sprendimą, piko metu net 88 proc. elektros energijos Lietuvoje buvo būtent gaminama Ignalinos atominėje elektrinėje. Tai buvo priimta ne dėl Lietuvos, bet dėl visos Europos saugumo. Todėl Lietuvai tai buvo labai brangus sprendimas, bet jis buvo būtent priimtas dėl mūsų visų. Šių darbų mes negalime sustabdyti pusiaukelėje dėl nepakankamo finansavimo. Ir žmonės, kurie kiekvieną dieną dirba Ignalinoje, jie taip pat turi turėti užtikrintumą dėl rytojaus. Galų gale, kai mes kalbame apie atominį objektą, jo saugumas yra aukščiausias reikalavimas. Ir šią savaitę virš Lietuvos NATO naikintuvai, ir dėkoju Italijos kolegoms, numušė droną. Tai dar kartą primena, kad grėsmės keičiasi, todėl pirmą kartą siūlome labai aiškiai numatyti ir Ignalinos elektrinės apsaugą nuo dronų bei hibridinių grėsmių. Aš dėkoju visiems šešėliniams pranešėjams, kurie parėmė šią Europos Parlamento poziciją ir kviečiu balsuoti už.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, cardiovascular diseases, as you perfectly know, are the main cause of death in the European Union. Yet for far too long, cardiovascular health has not received the political attention it deserves. Now we are changing that. This report, alongside the Commission's Safe Hearts Plan, is a crucial part of that progress, and I am sure that this report is good and it is well balanced. Let me thank all of you, especially my shadows, for the valuable contribution and your willingness to find common ground.

Our message is very simple: we must improve the lives of people living with cardiovascular diseases, while we also have to do everything we can to prevent new cases. Therefore, I ask you to support our work and vote in favour of this report.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, today we have an opportunity to adopt the Parliament's first comprehensive report on women's health.

Earlier this morning, President von der Leyen reiterated Europe's commitment to equality, and she also referenced backsliding in terms of women's rights itself. What better way to do that than ensuring that all genders have equal access to healthcare, that they are treated sensitively with respect and dignity, and that medical research recognises sex- and gender-based differences and invests sufficiently in understanding them?

The fact that women's symptoms and reports of pain are more likely to be dismissed, or the fact that it takes, on average, seven to ten years to diagnose endometriosis, or the fact that, in 2020, only 5 % of global research funding has been allocated to women's health – this is not equality and we need to address it today.

Some within this House have tried to weaponise this report to fuel their cultural wars, picking apart terminology and pitting one's community against another. But frankly, I find it ridiculous and shameful, and it simply distracts from the bigger picture, which is equality in health care. It is clear that your interests are not the interests of women, just divisiveness and political point-scoring. We need patient-centred healthcare, backed up by comprehensive research and training and funding.
Therefore, I urge you all to support this report and send the clear message to the citizens. Into your hands, Parliament, I commit this report, and I look forward to your support.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Herr Kommissar! Liebe Kolleginnen, liebe Kollegen! Wenn Mitgliedstaaten auf europäische Regelungen noch nationale Sondervorschriften draufsatteln, dann ist das nicht nur ein Bürokratieproblem, sondern auch ein Binnenmarktproblem. Wenn Brüssel gemeinsame Regeln beschließt und die Mitgliedstaaten bei der Umsetzung zusätzliche Pflichten draufsetzen, wird aus europäischem Recht wieder ein nationaler Flickenteppich. Für einen Konzern ist das nur teuer und lästig, für einen Mittelständler ohne eigene Compliance-Abteilung wird es zur unüberwindbaren Markteintrittsbarriere.

Nur ein Beispiel: Die Richtlinie über Elektroabfälle schreibt keinen monatlichen Meldezyklus vor. Das Land, das ich am besten kenne, verlangt ihn trotzdem – bis zum 15. des Folgemonats. Aus einer europäischen Vorgabe werden so zwölf Meldeprozesse im Jahr. Das bindet Zeit, Personal, schafft Kosten und schafft kein höheres Schutzniveau.

Auch in der Finanzmarktregulierung sehe ich diese Probleme. Auch wieder ein Beispiel aus meinem Land: Die Bundesanstalt für Finanzdienstleistungsaufsicht war die erste, die mit ESG-Anforderungen um die Ecke kam, bevor wir in Europa überhaupt darüber beraten haben. Man wollte Vorreiter sein, hat den Markt aber nur verwirrt.

Das sind klassische Beispiele dafür, wie es nicht laufen darf. Aber lassen Sie mich auch ganz klar sagen, nicht jede nationale Abweichung ist auch unzulässig. Oft lässt der europäische Gesetzgeber bewusst einen Spielraum bei der nationalen Umsetzung. Selbst bei Verordnungen geben wir den Mitgliedstaaten noch Spielräume zur Interpretation und Ausgestaltung, um Besonderheiten Rechnung zu tragen. Das Ziel kann aber natürlich nicht sein, dass die Mitgliedstaaten dann weit über das europäische Recht hinausgehen und den Harmonisierungsgedanken im Prinzip ad absurdum treiben.

Der Binnenmarkt ist das große Pfund, mit dem Europa wuchern kann. Er ist unsere Chance, um mit den USA und mit China mitzuhalten; er ist die Grundlage für Wachstum, für Skalierung, für Wohlstand und damit auch für soziale Sicherheit in ganz Europa. Doch die Idee des Binnenmarktes funktioniert nur, wenn nicht aus einer Regel 27 nationale Regeln werden, die sich zum Teil dann im Binnenmarkt auch wieder widersprechen. Jetzt muss das endlich auch einmal angegangen werden.

Heute Vormittag hat die Kommissionspräsidentin in ihrer Rede zur Lage der Europäischen Union dieses Thema ja auch selbst benannt. Wer beim Bürokratieabbau ernst macht, braucht einen Pakt gegen Gold-Plating. Das ist die richtige Diagnose, aber sie muss jetzt auch politische Konsequenzen haben. Diese Ankündigung darf nicht bloß eine Aufforderung bleiben an die Mitgliedstaaten, sondern es ist auch eine Aufforderung, Herr Kommissar, an die Kommission, die ja zu prüfen hat, wie die Mitgliedstaaten europäisches Recht in nationales Recht übersetzen.

Deshalb erwarte ich von der Kommission, dass sie sich dieses Problems nun wirklich annimmt und nicht nur die Situation beobachtet oder beschreibt, sondern wirklich handelt. Wenn Mitgliedstaaten ohne triftigen Grund draufsatteln, braucht es klare Konsequenzen, klare Fristen, verbindliche Nachbesserungen, die die Mitgliedstaaten liefern müssen, und wenn nötig auch ein Vertragsverletzungsverfahren gegen unbegründete nationale Zusatzlasten.

Wir sollten ehrlich sein: Was ein Mitgliedstaat draufsattelt, darf er hinterher auch nicht als Brüsseler Bürokratie kritisieren. Am Ende geht es um Vertrauen: Unternehmen investieren dort, wo sie sich auf Regeln verlassen können, nicht dort, wo sie in 27 Rechtsordnungen 27 Mal herausfinden müssen, was eine europäische Vorgabe eigentlich in einem Land auch wirklich bedeutet. Wer den Binnenmarkt stärken will, muss diese Verlässlichkeit zur politischen Priorität machen und nicht nur zu einer Fußnote.
Lassen Sie uns deswegen das Versprechen eines echten europäischen Binnenmarktes einlösen. Dafür trägt die Kommission Verantwortung, aber mit Verlaub, auch wir als Europäisches Parlament.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Commissioner, gold-plating occurs when EU law is transposed or implemented in a way that brings requirements, reporting obligations or procedures that exceed what is set out in EU legal acts.

As a result, it undermines the very purpose of the single market, which is to ensure the free movement of goods, services, capital and people through harmonisation, predictability and a level playing field.

SMEs – and they represent the vast majority of all of our companies – bear the brunt of single market barriers. For example, the single market strategy calls out EU rules as becoming overly complex and overlapping, resulting in high compliance costs and other avoidable administrative burdens.

Small companies often lack the personnel required to assess and ensure compliance with duplicate or divergent EU and national rules. Therefore, the way in which Member States transpose and apply EU law is one of a number of factors in determining whether our simplification agenda succeeds or fails in practice, particularly with SMEs.

The Commission identified the lack of single market ownership by the Member States as one of the 'terrible ten' barriers in the single market strategy. These barriers are often unintended consequences of real policy concerns by Member States, but they can be created by a lack of transposition and incorrect transposition, or unnecessarily divergent or burdensome implementation of Union law.
For these reasons, our efforts on the simplification agenda risk being thwarted if 27 different national transpositions bring back burdens afterwards.
The topic is significant for our economy and our competitiveness, and therefore it is a regular feature of our discussions in the Council, and indeed at the level of the European Council.

Let me recall that, in March, our leaders called on the Commission, the co-legislators and the Member States to continue to ambitiously simplify rules and reduce the administrative burden at EU, national and regional level, to ensure a regulatory framework that is both innovation- and SME-friendly, including by applying the 'think small first' principle, and without undermining predictability, EU policy goals, high standards, or the integrity of the market.

Since February 2025, the Commission and Commissioner Dombrovskis have presented 12 simplification proposals, known of course as the Omnibus packages, with the shared objectives of lowering costs and obligations.
The Council is fully committed to this exercise, as we believe the Omnibus packages will deliver savings of around EUR 14 billion in recurrent administration costs.

The Council also looks at progress regularly being made on dismantling the terrible ten barriers, and it is really important to stop new barriers being created. Lots of ways exist to limit or avoid gold-plating – regulations instead of directives for legislation is probably the easiest approach. Enrico Letta in his report emphasises this, and, indeed, to our leaders and to the General Affairs Council he has also mentioned this as something that could work and should be done.

The Council supports the objective to make legislation simple by design, and obligations clear and predictable. We want to ensure that unnecessary complexity is not reintroduced during our national implementation. I want to ensure that the intended benefits are realised by businesses and SMEs.
So Member States should pay particular attention to preventing gold-plating when transposing EU law, with the Commission providing help of course when needed.
Tackling gold-plating is a joint effort. Every actor at every level has a role to play in eliminating unnecessary burdens.
So, in this regard, we welcome the Commission's announcement to provide a toolkit of best practices and criteria which are intended to help Member States identifying and avoiding gold-plating.
