paragraphs.text: Madam President, Mr Minister, honourable Members, thank you for this opportunity to discuss the issue of gold-plating right after the 2026 state of the Union address by President von der Leyen that also addressed this problem. I welcome the European Parliament's attention to this topic, which is highly relevant for the functioning of the single market and for businesses across the European Union.

The communication on a clearer, simpler and better enforced EU rulebook adopted this April, announced an initiative to tackle the issue of regulatory gold-plating. It follows up on a single market strategy and the identification of terrible ten most harmful barriers. And I would like to quote the President von der Leyen from earlier today in this House: 'Yes, we are doing our best at the European level to cut red tape, but now it's time for Member States to step up'. If we are serious about simplification, we also need a pact against gold-plating. Gold-plating happens when a Member State, when transposing or implementing EU law in a given policy area, introduces wider scope, stricter rules or obligations that go beyond the requirements set in the EU legal act. Creating more burdensome procedures than what is necessary to implement EU law can also be considered gold-plating.

Gold-plating is problematic for several reasons. Divergent national rules create uneven conditions for businesses across Member States. This may distort competition and fragment the single market. Excessive national requirements may also increase compliance costs, especially for SMEs, and can discourage cross-border activity and undermine competitiveness. Large firms can often absorb complexity. SMEs cannot. This is why simplification is also a fairness issue.

As today's debates show, the issue of gold-plating is high on the political agenda. It is part of the broader simplification agenda, but also linked to the 'One Europe, One Market' roadmap. And it follows up on the European Council of 19 March, which called on Member States to avoid gold-plating and disproportionate national requirements. Unlawful gold-plating can be addressed through enforcement action, for example, when it leads to national legislation being incompatible with the directive. But often gold-plating relates to national policy choices or practices that are not contrary to the EU law but still undermine the single market and are harming businesses. This is why action is needed beyond enforcement of EU law. Subsidiarity is an essential principle, but it should not be used to increase bureaucracy. It is a matter of striking the right balance.
The Commission will therefore work closely with the Member States to pursue three objectives: better detection, better follow up and, of course, better prevention.

For better detection of gold-plating, we aim to use stakeholder consultations, for example through implementation dialogues held by Commissioners. Investigations under the Commission's single market focus areas for enforcement will also help detect instances of gold-plating.

For better identification, as well as better follow up, the European Semester and the Single Market Enforcement Task Force and the Single Market Sherpas can be leveraged further. This year, the European Semester spring package and country specific recommendations include more references to national barriers to the single market, including gold-plating. This analysis will be deepened further next year.

In any case, tackling gold-plating depends on the participation of Member States. This is why the Commission is preparing a toolkit with an overview of best practices to support Member States in detecting and preventing gold-plating.
As a first step, we have recently circulated a questionnaire to the Member States to gather information on national approaches as well as a survey to stakeholders.

Finally, the Commission will also take into consideration the risk of gold-plating when making legislative proposals, and formulate them in a manner that minimises that risk. For example, prioritising regulations over directives where appropriate and comprehensively addressing the matter being legislated can reduce room for gold-plating. The co-legislators, therefore, also have an important role to play here.
Thank you very much and I look forward for today's debate.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President. Commissioner, Minister, we need to simplify Europe because European entrepreneurs are frustrated today.

They are actually doing two jobs: one which they like, meaning they are building their businesses, they are serving their customers and they are creating new jobs. But then there is the other job they are doing: dealing with reporting, with compliance, with documentation and with growing bureaucracy. And that is why we need to simplify Europe.

That means three things. The first one is to truly introduce the 'one in, two out' principle: for every added euro in costs from new legislation, two have to be removed. Then we need to change and simplify faster. Today, businesses do not feel that we are delivering simplification and that has to change. And thirdly, stop the gold-plating. Cutting red tape in Brussels means little if capitals add new layers at home. Red tape is red tape, no matter where it comes from.
So less bureaucracy, more time to build, to hire and to innovate. Simplify Europe: that is my commitment to the 25 million entrepreneurs of Europe.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the S&D Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, Commissioner and Minister, it's very clear that unnecessary bureaucracy creates a disproportionate burden on our European SMEs. Our single market needs one set of rules, common standards and a level playing field. And therefore, we must put an end to gold‑plating, where the national transposition of EU laws creates unnecessary red tape with no added value. And it's good that President von der Leyen recalled that Member States have a primary responsibility to ensure that EU rules are implemented simply, effectively and proportionately.

But let us be clear: simplification must never become a race to the bottom. Higher standards do not equal bureaucracy when they deliver stronger rights, greater social security, and better protection for people, businesses and the environment. We do not need weaker regulation; we need smarter regulation. And safeguarding the integrity of the single market means ensuring that compliance is clear and accessible, and never asking workers, consumers or our climate to pay the price of deregulation.
We, as socialists and democrats, want European businesses to innovate, to grow, to compete globally. And protecting them means investing in Europeans' futures.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Megszámolni sem tudom, hogy hány vitát folytattunk le már ebben a Házban a bürokráciacsökkentés jegyében. Ezzel az a baj, hogy sok a beszéd és kevés az eredmény. A 383 Draghi-ajánlásból nem egész 16%-ot sikerült teljesen végrehajtani. Habár ezek egy részét nem osztom, az alacsony teljesítés jól mutatja, hogy a Bizottság és e Ház többsége bort iszik és vizet prédikál. Önök a baloldali néppárti nagykoalícióban csak beszélnek bürokráciacsökkentésről. Nem is csoda, hiszen pontosan Önök szavazták meg ezeket a lebontandó szabályokat. A deregulációt szitokszónak tartják, pedig nem elég az egyszerűsítés, sokkal kevesebb szabályra volna szükség.

A Néppárt rájött, hogy arcvesztés nélkül nem tudja teljesíteni a választási ígéretét, ezért most von der Leyen asszonnyal közösen azt találta ki, hogy azért nagy a teher, mert a tagállamok túlszabályoznak. Kérem, hagyják abba a felelősség áthárítását, legyen bátorságuk kimondani, hogy uniós szintű deregulációra van szükség. Csak így lesz Európában üzletbarát környezet és versenyképesség. Mi, patrióták ezért küzdünk.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, in dit debat over overregulering gaat het over een hardnekkig probleem: lidstaten die Europese regels onnodig streng interpreteren en daarmee de concurrentiepositie van bedrijven ernstig ondermijnen.

In mijn eigen land liggen de voorbeelden voor het oprapen. Ik denk aan de beslissing om heel Nederland in het kader van de nitraatrichtlijn als kwetsbaar aan te merken. Geen Europese verplichting, Nederland deed het toch. Gevolg: veehouders die aanhikken tegen enorme mestafzetkosten. Ik denk ook aan de Nederlandse stikstofnormen, die veel strenger zijn dan in omliggende landen. Gevolg: talloze boerenbedrijven die in hun voortbestaan worden bedreigd. En zo kan ik nog wel even doorgaan.

Laten we stoppen met nationale koppen. Ze brengen het gelijke speelveld ernstig in gevaar. Ik weet dat we landen niet kunnen dwingen af te zien van strengere regels, maar laten we de landen er op zijn minst op aanspreken.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, our single market remains fragmented and national gold-plating is one of the main causes.

Let's call it as it is: governments cannot blame Brussels bureaucracy while creating more bureaucracy themselves at home. They cannot demand simplification in Europe and then transform one European rule into 27 different national regimes, adding obligations, procedures and paperwork. That is political hypocrisy and our small and medium businesses pay the price.

Simplify, yes. Remove duplication and unnecessary reporting, yes. But simplification must not mean weaker protection for businesses and consumers. So stop gold-plating, implement what we decide together faithfully, on time and without national bureaucratic extras, and enforce it equally everywhere.

The single market was created to eliminate national barriers, not to allow governments to rebuild them through bureaucracy. One market, common rules, no national gold-plating, that is the simplification Europe needs.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, the ACRES environmental scheme in Ireland is the most complex environmental scheme we have seen. That's according to DG ENVI.

I'm not here to argue that the scheme shouldn't be so complex: Irish farmers are well educated and if paid well enough for the scheme, which they're not, then they would deal with the complexity. I don't want to hear, 'Well, we had a record number of people sign up to it.' They have no other option to get money, why wouldn't they sign up to it? They have no other option.

What I want to know is: why don't government politicians have the backbone to defend the decisions they've made? I've heard government politicians criticise the EU for decisions that our own Government had made and on this scheme, they had blamed Europe. To me there is a massive danger in that, because what happens is, you end up with people becoming Eurosceptics like myself. I got elected here believing loads of bad decisions were made by Europe, when in fact they were made by your government.
So if you're going to gold-plate, own it and take responsibility for it, otherwise you will destroy the European Union if you don't own what you do.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Meine Damen und Herren! Diese Debatte ist dringend notwendig. Als SME Europe der EVP fordern wir seit Langem, dass unser Mittelstand hier endlich gehört wird. Das sogenannte Gold‑Plating, also wenn Mitgliedstaaten bei der Umsetzung von EU‑Recht noch zusätzlich nationale Pflichten on top draufsetzen, kostet unsere Unternehmen Zeit und Geld und ist wettbewerbsschädlich. Dass Kommissionspräsidentin von der Leyen heute in ihrer Rede zur Lage der Union einen Pakt gegen Gold‑Plating gefordert hat, zeigt: Das Problem ist längst auf höchster europäischer Ebene angekommen.

Und gerade Deutschland liefert leider besonders viele Beispiele dafür, warum dieser Schritt notwendig ist. Wenn wir uns konkrete Beispiele anschauen, zeigt sich immer wieder: Zusätzliche Belastungen entstehen häufig nicht durch höhere Schutzstandards, sondern durch zusätzliche Verfahren. Schauen Sie auf das Verpackungsrecht: Deutschland koppelt die Registrierung unmittelbar daran, ob Produkte überhaupt in Verkehr gebracht werden dürfen. Und das, obwohl die europäischen Vorgaben diese konkrete Verknüpfung so nicht verlangen.

Wir müssen stärker auf das hören, was uns die KMU vor Ort zurückmelden. Die Praxis zählt. Die neue Simplification Platform der Kommission ist deshalb ein richtiger Schritt. Aber jetzt muss sie auch wirken! Wenn unsere Mitgliedstaaten über die europäischen Vorgaben hinausgehen, muss klar ausgewiesen werden: Was ist der EU‑Rechtskern, was ist nationale Zusatzregel und was kostet diese Zusatzregel unsere Unternehmen?

Das sogenannte Gold‑Plating, also wenn Mitgliedstaaten bei der Umsetzung von EU‑Recht noch zusätzlich nationale Pflichten on top draufsetzen, kostet unsere Unternehmen Zeit und Geld und ist wettbewerbsschädlich. Dass Kommissionspräsidentin von der Leyen heute in ihrer Rede zur Lage der Union einen Pakt gegen Gold‑Plating gefordert hat, zeigt: Das Problem ist längst auf höchster europäischer Ebene angekommen.

Und gerade Deutschland liefert leider besonders viele Beispiele dafür, warum dieser Schritt notwendig ist. Wenn wir uns konkrete Beispiele anschauen, zeigt sich immer wieder: Zusätzliche Belastungen entstehen häufig nicht durch höhere Schutzstandards, sondern durch zusätzliche Verfahren. Schauen Sie auf das Verpackungsrecht: Deutschland koppelt die Registrierung unmittelbar daran, ob Produkte überhaupt in Verkehr gebracht werden dürfen. Und das, obwohl die europäischen Vorgaben diese konkrete Verknüpfung so nicht verlangen.

Wir müssen stärker auf das hören, was uns die KMU vor Ort zurückmelden. Die Praxis zählt. Die neue Simplification Platform der Kommission ist deshalb ein richtiger Schritt. Aber jetzt muss sie auch wirken! Wenn unsere Mitgliedstaaten über die europäischen Vorgaben hinausgehen, muss klar ausgewiesen werden: Was ist der EU‑Rechtskern, was ist nationale Zusatzregel und was kostet diese Zusatzregel unsere Unternehmen?

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Herr Kommissar, Herr Minister, meine Damen und Herren! Zunächst möchte ich mit einem häufigen Missverständnis ausräumen. Gold‑Plating ist nicht dasselbe wie höhere nationale Standards. Wenn Mitgliedstaaten bei der Umsetzung von EU‑Recht ungerechtfertigte zusätzliche administrative Anforderungen schaffen, dann müssen wir das selbstverständlich verhindern. Aber wenn ein Mitgliedstaat Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer, Verbraucherinnen und Verbraucher, Gesundheit und Umwelt besser schützen will, dann muss dieser Spielraum bei Umsetzung einer Richtlinie selbstverständlich erhalten bleiben.

Vereinfachung darf nicht zum Deckmantel für Deregulierung und Herabsetzung von Standards werden. Und wir müssen natürlich unnötige Bürokratie abbauen. Gerade für Kleinstunternehmen können dieselben administrativen Anforderungen eine wesentlich größere Belastung darstellen als für große Unternehmen. Deshalb brauchen wir für Kleinstunternehmen verhältnismäßige und gezielte Ausnahmen, wo sie sinnvoll sind. Insgesamt machen wir die Einhaltung der Regeln einfacher, aber nicht die Regelungen schwächer.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, c'est donc le PPE qui se plaint de la bureaucratie, sachant qu'il gouverne l'UE depuis 20 ans. Certes, nous devons alléger l'empilement des normes et des charges qui s'abattent sur nos PME et qui mettent l'Europe à l'arrêt. L'Omnibus I veut réduire la charge réglementaire de 35 %, soit, mais retrancher un tiers de cette folie normative ne suffira pas à recouvrer un environnement sain.

Le problème n'est pas seulement la surtransposition zélée des textes européens par les États, c'est d'abord la manie perverse de l'UE de s'insinuer partout. Je mets le PPE au défi de mettre un terme à cette rage réglementaire dont il est la première cause. Nous avons besoin de liberté.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, deregolamentare e semplificare non sono slogan: sono una necessità economica. Gli eccessi normativi prodotti dall'Unione europea, negli ultimi anni, non hanno soltanto imposto costi alle nostre imprese ma hanno anche ridotto lo spazio degli Stati membri per costruire politiche industriali adatte alle proprie economie.

Siamo d'accordo nel contrastare il gold plating e la sovraregolamentazione nazionale. Ma se l'onere nasce già a Bruxelles, non possiamo scaricarne la responsabilità sugli Stati membri. I dati ci dicono che l'industria soffre, le imprese chiudono, e troppo poche, ne nascono per sostituirle. E a pagare il prezzo più alto sono soprattutto le PMI, che rappresentano il 99% delle imprese europee e milioni di posti di lavoro.

Proprio mentre vogliamo rilanciare la manifattura europea, dobbiamo quindi cambiare metodo: regole proporzionate, un approccio realmente su misura per le PMI e più spazio all'innovazione e alla digitalizzazione.
Non possiamo chiedere alle nostre imprese di competere nel mondo mentre continuiamo a legare loro le mani in Europa. Se vogliamo cambiare rotta, i primi a farlo dobbiamo essere noi, qui a Bruxelles.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Mr Commissioner, dear colleagues, our entrepreneurs have ideas, talent and ambition, but they lack a business environment where these ideas can flourish. And that's on us: we make it hard for them with too heavy administrative burdens and then, in some Member States, we pile on another layer of national requirements and obligations. And SMEs are paying the highest price: higher compliance costs and countless hours spent on paperwork, instead of focusing on what they do best – build, innovate and create jobs.

The single market can simply cannot mean 27 different rulebooks. Fragmentation weakens our economy, discourages investments and, ultimately, makes Europe less competitive. If gold-plating continues, we will not solve our competitiveness issue because we will be standing in our own way.

So the message for Member States is clear: implement EU rules properly, but do not turn every European law into a national bureaucratic project. We need clarity, predictability and less red tape. This is how we make Europe more competitive.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I couldn't have said it better. Our businesses have to do two jobs at the same time at the moment. One is their real job, what they're doing, their profession. And the second one is to report on it. Just yesterday, I spoke to a friend who runs a bakery in Berlin, and because of European rules and their German interpretation, he is now currently considered a packaging producer because he dared to put his own logo on his bags, which means that now for every croissant that he sells, he has to report that in a database.

Colleagues, when a baker needs a compliance department, we are doing something wrong and we have lost the plot. It doesn't mean that we need to tune down our ambition when it comes to sustainability and saving the planet. Actually, we have to do more. And, for example, the single‑use plastic ban in supermarkets is an example of how we can achieve that. But we cannot, under any circumstance, overwhelm our businesses when we want to kickstart our economy.
Therefore, let's stop all gold‑plating. Let's have the same rules across the common market and save the planet.

paragraphs.text: Fru Formand! Jeg må sige, at jeg synes, det er en meget forenklet debat, der foregår her om gold plating. Jeg synes, at I glemmer, at lande, der går foran med beskyttelse af borgere, miljø, klima og natur kan være til stor fordel for os alle. Og det er ikke bare noget, jeg siger. Jeg har selv været med til at gennemføre et forbud mod hormonforstyrrende bisfenol A i Danmark. Vi gik foran, og så fulgte EU bagefter. Vi har haft indsatsen mod klimaskadelige e-gasser, f-gasser, hvor både Danmark og Østrig viste, at det er muligt at udfase dem. Vi var foregangslande, der drev udviklingen. Ting, der skete, fordi vi kunne have foregangslande.

Og det er den mulighed, som vi nu lægger op til at stoppe. Der vil jeg sige: at være bange for, at nogen går foran, er en rigtig dårlig idé. Det er jo netop den mangfoldighed og de muligheder, det giver, som faktisk kan være med til at skabe grobund for flere af EU's mange innovative virksomheder. Så at droppe muligheden for at gå foran er efter min mening både fjollet og forældet.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Meine Damen und Herren! Zwischen 2019 und 2024 wurden in der EU rund 13 000 Rechtsakte verabschiedet. Gesetzgebungsakte, delegierte Rechtsakte und 5 700 Durchführungsrechtsakte. Leider setzen Mitgliedstaaten wie mein eigener gerne noch zusätzliche Auflagen obendrauf.

Frau von der Leyen verspricht bis 2029, die Belastungen für Unternehmen um mindestens 25 % zu senken, für kleine und mittlere Unternehmen sogar um 35 %. Das Ziel: 37,5 Mrd. EUR weniger Verwaltungskosten pro Jahr. Doch allein in diesem Jahr kommen weitere Pflichten hinzu: CBAM, DAC8, die Lohntransparenzrichtlinie, der KI-Akt, die Verpackungsverordnung und der Cyber Resilience Act. In der Summe entstehen Berichtspflichten, Nachweispflichten, Prüfpflichten, Dokumentationspflichten und vor allem Kosten. Die meisten davon mit freundlicher Unterstützung der CDU, die heute dieses Thema auf die Tagesordnung gesetzt hat.

Bürokratieabbau misst sich nicht an neuen Omnibuspaketen und neuen Versprechen. Er misst sich daran, ob ein Unternehmer weniger Formulare ausfüllt, weniger Berater bezahlen muss und mehr Zeit für Mitarbeiter, Innovation und Kunden investieren kann. Wer 25 % weniger Bürokratie verspricht, muss endlich aufhören, mehr neue Bürokratie zu produzieren!

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, da, ce uimitor, PPE-ul, cel care conduce Uniunea Europeană, cel care o are pe doamna von der Leyen, cel care a făcut un congres în România în timpul pandemiei, unde nu s-a respectat nicio regulă, ca să o aleagă pe doamna von der Leyen, are tupeul să ne întrebe ce considerăm noi să mai facem cu birocrația.

În România, toate actele pe care le adoptăm aici devin de 100 de ori mai greu de implementat, pentru că avem dosare cu șină, avem șpagă de dat, pentru că este cea mai coruptă țară din Uniunea Europeană, șpagă care se mai împarte și cu cei de pe aici.

Și vă întreb: cum puteți dumneavoastră să implementați aceeași lege pentru mai multe națiuni care sunt total diferite, de la tradiție și istorie și concepții, iar în România, de exemplu, avem ciobani cărora le-ați omorât oile, le interziceți să mai exporte și acum îi condamnați la moarte, iar ieri, în Piața Victoriei, în fața Guvernului, guvern care este pus de dumneavoastră, de la Bruxelles, au bătut oierii, au bătut ciobanii, i-au gazat și i-au călcat în picioare. Asta este democrația Uniunii Europene.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Herr Kommissar! Ein Reisebüro mit 20 Beschäftigten − unmittelbar in unserem Nachbarland − braucht jetzt einen Datenschutzbeauftragten. Nicht weil Europa das verlangt, sondern weil das nationale Gesetz das fordert. Dasselbe Reisebüro in Österreich braucht es nicht. Und wen macht dieses Reisebüro schuldig? Natürlich Brüssel. Brüssel ist schuld. Das ist Gold‑Plating: Europa gibt den Rahmen, und die Mitgliedstaaten legen drauf. Das schadet unseren Betrieben, unserem Standort, und schädigt den Ruf Europas. Die Rechnung zahlt die gesamte Wirtschaft. Österreichs Betriebe verbringen viel Zeit mit Bürokratie, und diese fehlt dann beim Kerngeschäft.

Positiv anzumerken ist, dass Sie, Herr Kommissar, im April einen Maßnahmenkatalog gegen Gold‑Plating für die Mitgliedstaaten ins Leben gerufen haben. Bei jeder Umsetzung muss klar ausgewiesen werden: Was verlangt Europa, und was wird national drauf gesetzt? Denn dann kann die Chefin oder der Mitarbeiter sagen: Ja, okay, das ist Gold‑Plating, und das wollen wir nicht. Wir brauchen weniger Bürokratie.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Nationale Autonomie beschränken, das fordern hier gerade EVP, EKR, ID und ESN in diesem Parlament. Klingt absurd, ist es auch! Eine der größten Stärken der Europäischen Union ist doch eigentlich, dass wir Dinge gemeinsam angehen, und das heißt dann leider meistens auch, sich auf einen kleinen gemeinsamen Nenner zu einigen. Und jetzt wollen Sie, die immer nach Souveränität schreien, den Mitgliedstaaten das Recht nehmen, mehr Arbeitsschutz, mehr Klimaschutz, mehr Menschenrechtsschutz umzusetzen, anstatt sich darauf zu konzentrieren, wie die Umsetzung des europäischen Rechts für alle funktionieren könnte.

Sie sind es doch eigentlich immer, die Souveränität fordern, und deswegen verstehe ich das nicht und muss Sie fragen: Na was wollen Sie denn jetzt? Mehr Europa, weniger Europa, gar kein Europa? Diese Gleichung geht bei Ihnen nicht auf. Ich will das kurz ausrechnen: Für Sie bedeutet weniger europäisches Recht gleich weniger Bürokratie. Aber die Realität ist doch, wenn wir das europäische Recht zurückfahren, haben wir 27 einzelne Regelungen und 27 Mal mehr Bürokratie. Diese Rechnung geht nicht auf.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señores del Partido Popular Europeo, bienvenidos al camino de la desregulación.

Ahora falta pasar de las palabras a los hechos, porque hoy se suman al carro de la desregulación, pero el Partido Popular Europeo —junto con los socialistas, los verdes, etcétera— son los máximos responsables de la mayor asfixia regulatoria que sufren las empresas europeas. Además, no es coherente denunciar la sobrerregulación nacional mientras sigue intacto el monstruo burocrático que ustedes han creado con la señora Von der Leyen a la cabeza.
Nosotros decimos «no» a la sobrerregulación y decimos «sí» a la simplificación y a la recuperación de la prosperidad que han arrebatado a los europeos.
Señor comisario, si no saben cómo hacerlo, se pueden descargar el programa de desregulación de VOX —que está a su servicio— que es el único partido que se compromete...
(la presidenta interrumpe al orador)

Nosotros decimos «no» a la sobrerregulación y decimos «sí» a la simplificación y a la recuperación de la prosperidad que han arrebatado a los europeos.

Señor comisario, si no saben cómo hacerlo, se pueden descargar el programa de desregulación de VOX —que está a su servicio— que es el único partido que se compromete...

paragraphs.text: Fru talman! Jag tror vi är eniga om att saker och ting behöver förenklas. EU:s omnibusinitiativ är ju ett sådant förslag, och vi kan nog vara eniga om att de nationella myndigheterna är övernitiska i att uttolka de här EU-reglerna, som vi fattar beslut om här i kammaren.
Men det viktiga beslutet, eller det viktiga ställningstagandet här, är ju att vi måste vända kursen, vi måste avreglera. Vi måste vara öppna med att tala om avreglering.

Vissa regler, tunga regler, är nödvändiga och de ska vara väldigt väl utformade. Det är på det sättet som vi kan se till att underlätta för företag, verksamheter, att inte hamna i en överbyråkratiserad EU-massa av regler. Den vägen behöver vi gå.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Der Fisch fängt vom Kopf zu stinken an, das wissen wir alle. Nur in der EU, da stimmt das nicht immer. Viele Hürden und viel Aufwand, mit denen unsere Unternehmen tagtäglich beschäftigt sein müssen, die kommen nicht von der EU oder dem Kopf; die kommen daher, dass die 27 Flossen alle in irgendeine andere Richtung schwimmen wollen.

Wie absurd ist es zum Beispiel, dass in Österreich die Autos viel öfter zum Pickerl müssen als in anderen Ländern der EU, als ob sie in Österreich mehr Gefahr darstellen würden oder anders Verbrauchsspuren zeigen. Das ist nicht nur absurd, das ist tatsächlich auch eine Bürde für Menschen, aber auch für Unternehmen.

Gut, dass wir das jetzt ändern, aber noch besser, dass bereits elf Länder mit Österreich die Allianz für Entbürokratisierung eingegangen sind. Aber das heißt auch, dass da noch Platz ist – nämlich für 16 andere Länder, auch für Irland. Es ist Zeit, dass die 27 Flossen endlich in eine Richtung schwimmen und wir Europa leichter machen.

paragraphs.text: Pani predsedníčka, vážení kolegovia a kolegyne, som veľmi rada, že tu dnes máme túto debatu, pretože nie sú to NGO-ky – mimovládky, nie sú to aktivisti, ale sú to práve firmy, podniky a priemysel, ktorí sú chrbtovou časťou Európskej únie a ktorí naozaj nám pomáhajú dosiahnuť to, čo potrebujeme.

Dnes je pani predsedníčka Európskej komisie Ursula von der Leyenová. Prvé, čo hovorila, bol práve boj proti gold platingu a podpora malých a stredných podnikov, ale nepovedala úplne presne, že akým spôsobom to môžeme robiť.

Firmy, dnes aj malé firmy, majú stále nejaké nové zelené normy, ktoré tu prijímame, majú stále viac a viac reportingu, musia stále viac a viac formulárov vyplňovať. Musia kontrolovať svojich dodávateľov a podobne.

Keď nastupovala táto Komisia, tak bolo sľúbené, že ak prijmeme nejakú novú legislatívu, bude sa robiť audit tej súčasnej legislatívy a že za každú jednu novú legislatívu nejaká iná sa odstráni. Ja sa chcem spýtať Európskej komisie, kde je toto pravidlo a koľko takýchto zbytočných zákonov už zatiaľ Európska komisia a Európska únia odstránila. Pretože toto je skutočne to, ako môžeme pomôcť firmám v Európskej únii.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhor Ministro, Senhor Comissário, a concretização do mercado único é essencial para que possamos atingir os nossos objetivos enquanto União Europeia. Para termos um mercado único, é absolutamente fundamental que haja igualdade de concorrência entre as várias empresas dentro do espaço europeu. Ao que nós temos assistido é à criação de barreiras, em vez da eliminação dessas mesmas dificuldades.

Com um conjunto de regras europeias que muitas vezes têm como propósito a redução dessa mesma burocracia, o que acontece, não menos vezes, é que os próprios países aproveitam o processo de transposição dessas diretivas para criar dificuldades, para criar obstáculos, numa dinâmica protecionista de cada um dos mercados internos. Pois bem, a proteção do mercado interno de cada país não casa com a proteção do mercado único, que é europeu.

E nós queremos ser competitivos à escala global. Hoje de manhã, ouvimos a senhora presidente da Comissão falar em competitividade. E essa mesma competitividade pressupõe que, em primeiro lugar, os 450 milhões de habitantes da União Europeia possam ser servidos por um único mercado. Só assim nós conseguiremos ser mais fortes, mais resistentes. Só a união no propósito de construir um mercado que seja um mercado europeu alimentará a vontade de sermos resilientes a nível global.

paragraphs.text: Sinjura President, meta nitkellmu dwar il-kompetittività Ewropea, irridu nibdew minn realtà sempliċi: għal negozju żgħir, kull proċedura għandha prezz. Prezz fil-ħin, fil-flus, fil-ġiri bejn uffiċċji, accountants u esperti differenti. Kull siegħa li sid ta' negozju jqatta' jimxi ma' proċeduri li ma jżid l-ebda protezzjoni, hija siegħa li ma jkunx jista' jinvesti fin-negozju tiegħu.

U għalhekk is-simplifikazzjoni hija meħtieġa. Imma rridu nkunu ċari dwar dan xi jfisser. Ma tfissirx li nnaqqsu l-protezzjoni tal-konsumatur, tal-ħaddiema jew tal-ambjent. Tfisser li nneħħu dak li huwa doppju, mhux meħtieġ jew sproporzjonat. Ir-regoli Ewropej għandhom jagħtu ċertezza lin-negozji u protezzjoni liċ-ċittadin. Ix-xogħol tagħna huwa li nagħmlu aktar faċli biex l-SMEs tagħna jinvestu, jadattaw u jikbru mingħajr ma nnaqqsu l-istandards li l-Ewropa hija mibnija fuqhom. Għax Ewropa kompetittiva mhijiex Ewropa b'inqas regoli, imma hija Ewropa b'regoli aħjar.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Szanowni Państwo! Europejska Partia Ludowa, największa siła w Parlamencie Europejskim, zwołuje debatę o walce z biurokracją. Żałosna komedia. To nie jest troska o firmy. To wasza próba wybielenia wizerunku, który Europejczycy coraz częściej dostrzegają.

To wy, przez lata, z socjalistami i zielonymi dławiliście europejską gospodarkę. To wy przez dekadę głosowaliście za lawiną dyrektyw: Zielony Ład, sprawozdawczość, polityka klimatyczna. To wy zawiesiliście kamień u szyi każdej firmie, która jeszcze chce w Europie coś produkować. To wy stworzyliście ten system – system żerowania na pracy i przedsiębiorczości Europejczyków.

Ta sama hipokryzja jest w Polsce. W Brukseli dzisiaj krzyczycie „stop regulacjom”, a w Warszawie jutro będziecie dalej „dokręcać” unijne przepisy i nękać nimi małe i średnie przedsiębiorstwa. Jednego dnia płaczecie w Parlamencie Europejskim nad losem firm, a drugiego – w Warszawie i innych europejskich stolicach tacy jak wy zaciskać będą biurokratyczną pętlę jeszcze bardziej.

Przedsiębiorcy nie potrzebują kolejnej debaty. Wasze kłamliwe słowa nic nie zmienią. Potrzeba twardej reformy politycznej i odrzucenia waszej niszczycielskiej polityki. Inaczej za kilka lat z Europy będą gospodarcze ruiny.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, economische groei: dat is de prioriteit van de EU om welvaart en welzijn te bestendigen. Kmo's zijn daarvoor cruciaal, maar onduidelijke regels en verschillende implementaties maken het voor hen onmogelijk om de vruchten van een eengemaakte markt te plukken. In kleinere lid- en deelstaten is het vaak nog ingrijpender: bedrijven in een kleine economie hebben minder ruimte om extra administratieve lasten en afwijkende nationale regels op te vangen.

Hoe pakken we dit nu aan? Ten eerste moet de EU in de eerste plaats zorgen voor duidelijke en rechtszekere regels die niet voor interpretatie vatbaar zijn. Ten tweede: minder regels en minder administratieve lasten, zodat ondernemers kunnen ondernemen. En ten derde moet de Commissie duidelijk in kaart brengen welke regels lidstaten extra opleggen, waarvoor soms een goede reden is, maar ook welke gevolgen die hebben voor grensoverschrijdende activiteiten. Raadpleegbaar voor iedereen. Pak het aan, commissaris.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, especially today, blaming the EU seems to be quite fashionable, and I must admit that I also quite often do that. But if one puts aside the bad mood, and the populism heard, especially in the morning, it has not been a failure to agree, for example, about the inner market.
Obviously, nothing is perfect that's been made by people, but it is not a minor thing to have a 100 million inhabitants larger inner market than the United States has, for example.
The decisions taken at the parliamentary level are not perfect. They are compromises which usually everyone criticises, but still they reflect the majority.

What I do hope are the legislational frameworks to be flexible enough for the Member States, and, for the Member States, encouragement to use the flexibilities agreed. And this is not at all often tested, for example, in my Nordic home state of Finland.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Fragmentacja rynku, która jest właśnie skutkiem nadmiernej regulacji, kosztuje naszą gospodarkę setki miliardów euro rocznie. Dzisiaj na stole – jak wyliczają eksperci – leży 713 miliardów euro, jeśli skończymy z tą praktyką.

Celem europejskiego prawa musi być harmonizacja przepisów, tak aby nasze gospodarki mogły sprawnie funkcjonować. I weźmy prosty przykład: jeżeli ciężarówka może ważyć do 44 ton w Belgii, a tylko do 40 ton we Francji, to musi zatrzymać się na granicy i towary również. Zakładamy, że dzięki Schengen granice przestały być barierami, ale w praktyce wciąż nie osiągnęliśmy tego celu. Zbyt często państwa członkowskie, wdrażając prawo unijne, dodają własne normy i procedury administracyjne. I zamiast prostych, jednolitych zasad otrzymujemy jeszcze więcej biurokracji dla przedsiębiorców, dla obywateli.

Dlatego jednym z priorytetów zespołu „Sprawdzamy” było ograniczenie tego zjawiska. W Polsce zidentyfikowaliśmy około 100 przypadków, w których właśnie Polska za rządów PiS-u przyjęła bardziej restrykcyjne przepisy, niż wymagało tego prawo unijne. I dzisiaj nasz rząd podejmuje działania, by to zmienić. Nasza siła tkwi w jednolitości rynku. Polska dzisiaj przewodzi w walce z nadmierną regulacją i nadszedł czas, aby inne państwa członkowskie poszły w nasze polskie ślady.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, è giusto porci l'obiettivo di ridurre la burocrazia per le imprese. Ma lo dico subito ai colleghi della destra: giù le mani dalle tutele per i lavoratori e dal modello sociale europeo.

Con la direttiva sul lavoro tramite piattaforme abbiamo lasciato agli Stati lo spazio per dare maggiori tutele su condizioni di lavoro e gestione algoritmica. Così come con il regolamento sull'intelligenza artificiale, per evitare un Grande Fratello digitale nei luoghi di lavoro, lo stesso dovrà valere per la revisione degli appalti pubblici. Regole comuni, sì, ma gli Stati devono poter andare oltre sulle tutele sociali e ambientali.

Noi siamo per l'armonizzazione europea e crediamo nelle regole comuni. paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, oggi finalmente parliamo di piccole imprese, di artigiani, di quelli che avete colpevolmente dimenticato, mai ascoltati quando scrivete i provvedimenti, sempre vessati da costi e burocrazia, purtroppo, insostenibili.
Avete preferito le logiche delle lobby e delle grandi industrie, che peraltro sono fallite anch'esse, dimenticando la peculiarità del made in Italy che ha reso grande l'Italia e l'Europa.

E questa mattina la Presidente von der Leyen ci ha annunciato di fatto un nuovo Green Deal. È il terrore? Ma non vi bastano i danni che avete già fatto? Volete davvero che le nostre imprese chiudano tutte?

Noi vogliamo e combattiamo, certo, per un'Unione europea unita sì, ma diversa: più nazioni, meno ideologia, meno burocrazia, energia a costi sostenibili e regole costruite sulla realtà delle nostre imprese.
Se soffocate chi produce, non state salvando l'Europa: la state condannando al declino.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Komisarzu! Panie Ministrze! Gold-plating stał się zmorą naszej Unii, w tym także Polski. Rok temu polskie organizacje pracodawców opublikowały raport, w którym opisano 100 konkretnych przypadków nadregulacji. Nadregulacji, które zniechęcają do zakładania biznesu, zatrudniania ludzi i prowadzenia nowych inwestycji. Konieczny jest przegląd prawa krajowego, by usunąć takie przeszkody.

Tak, potrzebujemy dziś paktu przeciw gold-platingowi, o czym mówiła rano przewodnicząca von der Leyen. Dlaczego? Dlatego, że dziś jako cała Unia działamy w realiach kryzysu. My, reprezentanci instytucji unijnych i parlamentów krajowych, mamy nie więcej niż 12 miesięcy, by pokazać naszym przedsiębiorcom, że potrafimy im pomóc poprzez wprowadzanie zachęt inwestycyjnych, upraszczanie przepisów, obniżanie cen prądu.

Inaczej staniemy się poddostawcami i podwykonawcami firm chińskich i amerykańskich. Mamy jeszcze czas, by uratować nasze MŚP i miejsca pracy, by zatrzymać w Europie najlepsze talenty. Każdy, kto zasiada w tej Izbie, powinien to uznać za nasze zadanie nr 1.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, llevamos ya unos cuantos paquetes ómnibus que —estamos viendo— se están demostrando absolutamente insuficientes, básicamente por su falta de ambición.

Y mientras tanto, aquí y también en los Parlamentos nacionales, dedicamos nuestro tiempo a regular para introducir más cargas, más obligaciones, más trámites, más burocracia a las empresas, como también hemos visto aquí con ocasión de la trasposición de normas comunitarias.

En ese sentido aplaudimos el anuncio que esta mañana hacía la presidenta de la Comisión de ese pacto contra la sobrerregulación. Pero, ojo, el pacto no puede quedarse en una simple declaración de buenas intenciones por parte de los firmantes.

Para que el pacto tenga sentido, debe incluir el compromiso firme de los Estados y de la Comisión. De los Estados para asumir el principio, en primer lugar, de que una carga se crea, una carga se elimina. En segundo lugar, para asumir, también por parte de los Estados, la obligación de realizar estudios de impacto de aquellas normas de transposición de carácter económico o medioambiental sobre las pequeñas y medianas empresas. En tercer lugar, el compromiso también de los Estados para que las normas de transposición incluyan un anexo en el que se especifique claramente qué parte es transposición y qué parte es aportación de cada uno de los Estados. Y, por último —en la lógica— el compromiso de la Comisión para, por un lado, lógicamente, hacer seguimiento de los procesos de transposición, pero también para exigir responsabilidades en caso de incumplimiento.
Porque, señorías, concluyo: simplificar no es desregular, simplificar es regular mejor manteniendo los estándares.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Fru talman! Ja, ni pratar gärna om avreglering, men för mig handlar det här om lokal demokrati.

I Avesta har kommunen sagt: På vår mark ska det vara seriösa företag som får bygga. Man ska ha kollektivavtal, sjysta löner och villkor. Men det kravet har domstolen stoppat och hänvisar till EU-rätten.

Det här handlar om vem som ska få bestämma hur vi löser våra problem. Vi har lokala kommunpolitiker, folkvalda. Vi har 349 riksdagsledamöter som svenska folket har valt för att stifta våra lagar. Då är det orimligt om de gång på gång ska mötas av svaret "EU tillåter inte det".

Vi ser det här bland annat när vi försöker bekämpa arbetslivskriminaliteten. Vi ser det när vi vill kunna välja lokalt odlad mat till skolbarn och patienter. Och det riskerar vi att se ännu mer av om vi i den här kammaren trycker på för mer strikta EU-regler och gör det till ett självändamål att samma regel ska genomföras exakt lika överallt.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, la dérive normative qui afflige l'Europe est particulière dans les régions ultrapériphériques où l'application des directives relève du sabotage économique et social.

Les entreprises, les agriculteurs et les pêcheurs ultramarins étouffent sous des contraintes environnementales et des réglementations phytosanitaires conçues pour le continent européen. Dès lors, comment les entreprises ultramarines pourraient-elles être compétitives dans leur environnement régional?

Les RUP n'en peuvent plus de cette folie normative, et je me réjouis que la nouvelle vision stratégique présentée par le vice-président Fitto commence enfin à y apporter un début de réponse. Mais d'autres simplifications sont encore nécessaires: lorsque des projets européens sont entérinés, il faut que les bénéficiaires puissent compter, dans la longue phase de déblocage des fonds, sur la garantie de l'UE. Sans quoi, par une inconséquence administrative coupable, les plus belles initiatives finiront mort-nées.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, un fardeau administratif terrible pèse sur nos PME. Soyons honnêtes, les textes votés ici sont souvent déconnectés de la réalité, voire totalement dingues. C'est le cas du pacte vert, texte nocif que mon groupe des Patriotes pour l'Europe a combattu sans relâche car il organise la décroissance européenne.

Mais certains États aggravent encore les choses: en France, la technocratie parisienne sabote notre souveraineté nationale en surtransposant vos normes. Quand l'Europe autorise, Paris interdit, plongeant nos paysans dans une concurrence mortifère et asphyxiant nos PME. Cette folie est encore pire dans nos territoires ultramarins, écrasés par des contraintes inadaptées. Les autres victimes de ce rouleau-compresseur sont nos collectivités. Sur le terrain, nos maires font un boulot héroïque. Face à eux, l'administration se comporte comme une mante religieuse: elle paralyse l'action locale pour la dévorer sous la paperasse. Simplifions les marchés publics pour leur permettre de commander directement aux entreprises de leur territoire.

Enfin, j'alerte ce Parlement: le prochain budget européen risque d'être vérolé par la gauche avec les conditionnalités du budget genré et le principe consistant à «ne pas causer de préjudice important». J'appelle le PPE à se réveiller: ne donnez pas vie à ce délire, cessez de céder aux folies socialistes et redonnons du bon sens à l'Europe et à la France.

Ebben Brüsszel és a tagállamok azonban idáig kudarcot vallottak. A sorozatos ígéretek ellenére a kkv-kat sújtó bürokratikus terhek egyre csak nőnek. Ezt jelzi, hogy egyre több kisvállalkozás kényszerül arra, hogy munkaerejének több mint 10%-a adminisztratív feladatokat végezzen, ami elfogadhatatlan.

Aggályos az energiaárak kérdése is. Ma egy európai kisvállalkozó két-háromszor fizet többet az áramért és négyszer-ötször a földgázért versenytársaihoz képest. Ilyen tehertétellel mind a versenyképesség, mind a nagyvállalattá történő átalakulás ellehetetlenül. Végül, elfogadhatatlan az is, hogy a kkv-k többsége a pályázati feltételek túlzott szigorúsága miatt nem jut célzott támogatásokhoz. interventions.speaker_label: Valdis Dombrovskis, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, minister, honourable Members, thank you for these useful comments and reflections.
In finding ways to tackle harmful gold-plating, we must keep in mind that this task is, first and foremost, the responsibility of Member States when implementing EU law.

The Commission will support Member States in avoiding gold-plating, for example by providing transposition guidance and the toolkit. We will also play an active role in detecting gold-plating when it occurs, and will cooperate with Member States to remove it. Where gold-plating is found to be illegal, the Commission will make use of its most powerful tool: infringement proceedings.
The European Parliament, as co-legislator, also has an important responsibility to reduce the opportunities for Member States to gold-plate.
In sum, the Commission aims to address gold-plating, with a focus on protecting the single market, minimising its detrimental effects on businesses, consumers and competitiveness as a whole.
As we finalise our toolkit and deepen our analysis on the single market barriers in the context of the European Semester, we hope to see real changes in the coming months and years.

interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I have to say this was a fantastic display of unity today, because I think nobody likes gold‑plating – nobody in this Chamber, nobody in the Council, nobody in the Commission – because it undermines the harmonisation and the smooth‑functioning of the single market, which is the backbone of all of our economies in which our SMEs operate. So the Presidency, of course, considers addressing this to be a crucial topic in Council discussions. But it is up to all of us as well. We are the legislators. If we see our Member States gold-plating, we should point this out and point out this is not the law that we passed here on behalf of the people in the European Union.

So all EU institutions must play their part in preventing and reducing gold‑plating and red tape, and ensuring that legislation is of a high quality and contains clear and unambiguous rules. The Council is fully committed to the 'One Europe, One Market' roadmap and to tackling the 'terrible ten' barriers. Reducing gold‑plating is a key element of that commitment.

interventions.speaker_label: Simon Harris, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Commissioner, I am honoured to present today the Council's position on the draft budget of the European Union for the financial year 2027. We have worked on the Commission's proposal since it was presented on 10 June, and I am pleased to report that, following a thorough examination, the Council adopted its position unanimously on 4 September.

I'd like to highlight three elements that we consider important. First, the budget must stand at an appropriate level for the implementation of policies and programmes. Second, it must safeguard our ability to cope with ongoing crises and challenges. And third, it must leave room for flexibility to deal with unforeseen circumstances – of which we have seen only too many in recent years.

To endure all of this, the Council's position provides for EUR 191.9 billion in commitment appropriations and EUR 202.1 billion in payment appropriations, excluding appropriations foreseen for special instruments outside the multiannual financial framework ceilings.

In line with the MFF mid-term revision, the budget for 2027 aims to safeguard key EU priorities: our capacity to respond to ongoing crises, notably in Ukraine and in the Middle East, to enhance defence readiness and preparedness, and to manage migration pressures. Guided by these priorities – which are endorsed by this Parliament – the Council's position has been carefully calibrated to ensure the Union continues to deliver on its commitments, while retaining the necessary flexibility to deal with unforeseen challenges in the coming year.

Let me continue by pointing out the main lines of our position. Looking at our programmes, they will deliver more than in 2026. However, the Council considers that some of the increases proposed by the Commission, compared to the voted budget of 2026, should be moderated. National finances are under pressure and the difficult fiscal situation of the Member States and the unforeseen challenges we have been facing in the recent years should also be taken into account. This is why these adjustments are made across the other budget headings.

Nevertheless, the Council also sees where certain programmes can be reinforced. In today's difficult geopolitical world, humanitarian aid cannot be overlooked. The Council has consequently increased the Commission's proposed allocation in Heading 6 for this.

Concerning the Union's ability to deal with unforeseen circumstances, we saw the need to limit the use of special instruments and to create additional margins, preserving resources for unforeseen circumstances and for future needs. On debt management, we support the Commission's proposal for the financing costs of the new Ukraine support loan.

We took a more cautious stance on the forecasted disbursements related to NextGenerationEU. Our approach to the financing costs of NextGenerationEU is fully consistent with the revised MFF Regulation, and reflects the agreement reached during the conciliation on the budgets for 2025 and 2026 with regard to the 50/50 approach to be applied annually. The Council's position also includes horizontal adjustments to some support expenditure lines, maintaining them at their 2026 levels.

Finally, turning to payments, the Council has not touched the payment of appropriations, apart from proportionate changes to the adjustments made in the commitments. The Council's recurrent objective is to ensure that the EU budget is managed prudently, responsibly and realistically, with a clear focus on achieving tangible results and delivering value for taxpayers' money, benefiting all Europeans.

This goes beyond political rhetoric: EU resources must be allocated to where they can have greatest impact, while safeguarding the Union's financial sustainability. Moreover, an effective and accountable use of the EU budget will not only strengthen the delivery of the Union's priorities, but will also reinforce citizens' trust in the very European Union.
I look forward to your comments and feedback today, and to a constructive dialogue with you today and in the weeks and months ahead. Thank you very much for your attention.

interventions.speaker_label: Piotr Serafin, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, dear Deputy Prime Minister, I would like to thank you for the presentation of the position of the Council on the draft budget for 2027. But, as you can also expect, it is an opportunity to share some reflections on your approach.

You will not be surprised to hear that, in our view, the cut of EUR 1 billion proposed by the Council is not justified. The Commission has prepared the draft budget for 2027 in a context of very limited availability and flexibilities. We should all be aware of these constraints. This is the last year of the current multiannual financial framework and the space for manoeuvre is very limited.
Our proposal is prudent, and addresses the current challenges to the extent possible. But, most importantly, it allows the EU to respect its commitments.

That is why we are concerned with the position of the Council. The cuts proposed by the Council target, for example, Horizon Europe, the flagship programme for research and development; Digital Europe and the Connecting Europe Facility, our common programmes to fund investments in digital and transborder infrastructure; Erasmus+, one of the most successful programmes for our students and researchers; EU4Health, strengthening our healthcare systems in all Member States. All programmes supporting rights and values at a time when they need to be protected as never before.
To be frank, we are confused and we do not understand the signal that the Council wanted to send with these cuts.

The Council position also includes a cut of EUR 180 million for the NGEU financing costs. Let me remind you that the draft budget delivers on a benchmark of 50 % already agreed together for the EURI cascade mechanism. We need to wait, of course, until the final data are available, but at this point this cut is, for sure, not justified.

On a positive note, let me say that we appreciate that the compromise on Heading 7– Administration – does not include major changes to the Commission proposal. This is a recognition of the efforts made by the Commission and all institutions to keep administrative spendings in check. We will continue these efforts, even if it is clear that administration will remain under substantial pressure. Some modifications to the final 2026 salary adjustment rate may be needed after the publication by Eurostat at the end of October.

I also want to underline that in its approach for financing the interest costs for the Ukraine support loan, the Commission has carefully assessed the existing budgetary availabilities and special instruments, while taking into account existing obligations and prudent budgeting.

In terms of next steps, the amending letter will include the updates of the needs for the EURI interest line – I referred to it already – the Ukraine support loan, and Heading 7. It will also include the usual update to agricultural expenditure.
Following the Parliament's reading, we will send the usual executability letter as an input to the Conciliation.
As always, we will do our best to facilitate the process and to reach a successful and timely outcome on the 2027 budget.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Minister Harris, Commissioner Serafin, colleagues, Europe faces several crises at once, and public finances are among them. No one in this Chamber would dispute that prudent budgeting is essential, and especially so for the EU budget.

Minister, thank you for the Council's position on the EU's draft general budget for 2027. We value it. It does, however, raise questions of method and of consistency. If I understand the method correctly, the Council took the 2026 figure for each line and, wherever the draft budget was high, simply cut it. Not on budgetary criteria such as absorption, not on political criteria such as lower priority; a top-down approach that ignores the needs and added value of individual programmes. It also does real damage to small budget lines and actually saves, at the same time, barely half a percent of the overall budget.

Allow me to quote the Presidency's own programme: 'We will support all efforts to respond to the exceptional energy crisis facing Europe'. And yet, the Connecting Europe Facility, the programme that builds on energy interconnections, is cut by EUR 47 million.

Another quote: 'Health innovation will be a central contributor to Europe's competitiveness and technological leadership'. And EU4Health is cut by EUR 41 million, after losing EUR 1 billion in the MFF revision. The Health Cluster of Horizon Europe loses a further EUR 74.5 million.

One more quote: 'We will advance educational mobility through Erasmus+'. Erasmus+ is cut by an additional EUR 159 million, after the Commission's own downward adjustment of EUR 357 million. An unusual way, if I may say so, of advancing educational mobility.

Horizon Europe, our flagship – heavily oversubscribed, with a measurable impact on growth and jobs – loses more than EUR 230 million in total. The Presidency plans to host an AI summit on empowering our people to thrive in a digital society. Meanwhile, Digital Europe loses EUR 55 million and the digital skills line is cut by more than a third.

Behind every one of these lines are our students, our researchers, our patients, our people – in Ireland, in Latvia, in every Member State. Minister, we are grateful for this position. It gives this House every reason to answer with a solid, united counter-proposal – real priorities instead of a sterile across-the-board haircut and, I trust, rather more consistent with the priorities of the Presidency itself. Dear shadow rapporteurs, political advisers and the budget secretariat: a demanding task lies ahead of us.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Commissioner, Minister Harris, welcome to the European Parliament and thank you for presenting the Council position on the draft general budget for the European Union for 2027.

With this debate, we are entering the final and particularly important stage of the budgetary procedure. As always, our responsibility is to find a European compromise while ensuring that the Union and its institutions have the resources necessary to deliver for European citizens.

The 2027 budgets come at a particularly challenging moment. It is the final year of the current MFF, and the pressure on the European budget has increased considerably over the past years. This is particularly evident under Heading 7, which finances the European public administration and the institutions of the Union. We have to be realistic about the need for efficiency and sound financial management. All institutions have a responsibility to use European taxpayers' money carefully, and they have to make significant efforts to improve efficiency, redeploy staff and identify savings.

As rapporteur for the other sections, I will continue to focus on the core functions of all the Union's institutions. The European Parliament, the Court of Justice, the Court of Auditors, the European Economic and Social Committee, the Committee of the Regions, the European Ombudsman, the European Data Protection Supervisor and the European External Action Service all have different responsibilities, but they share one fundamental requirement: they must have sufficient capacity to perform the tasks assigned to them in the service of the European citizens.

In particular, cybersecurity and physical security have become essential to the functioning of every European institution. The same applies to the development and responsible use of artificial intelligence. These are not optional investments. They are increasingly necessary conditions for the security, resilience and effective functioning of the Union's administration and for ensuring a safe working environment for those who serve our institutions. This is not about increasing expenditure for its own sake. It is about making sure that the Union's institutions can do the work that citizens, Member States and the European Parliament expect from them.

The final year of the current MFF should therefore be an opportunity to address the remaining structural pressures under Heading 7. I hope that through constructive negotiations between Parliament, the Council and the Commission, we will find a balanced solution that respects budgetary discipline while ensuring that the European institutions have the capacity to deliver on their responsibilities.

Our citizens expect European institutions that are effective, secure and capable of responding to the new challenges. It is our responsibility to make sure that the budget allows them to do precisely that.

paragraphs.text: A Uachtaráin, honourable Members, Commissioner, firstly, can I say thank you for this valuable and constructive exchange? Today's initial exchange and initial debate has shown that despite differing views on specific points, we do all share a common goal, and that common goal and duty is to establish a robust and effective European Union budget in a timely manner for 2027. And I very much look forward to the European Parliament's position on the budget for 2027, and I hope that that will allow for constructive, meaningful engagement on our respective positions, which will allow us to converge and reach a final agreement in November.

We look forward to entrust the Commission's role as an honest broker to bridge that gap between positions and to help develop balanced, compromised solutions. While I am presenting the Council's position today ‑ the unanimous Council's position ‑ our presidency's aim is defined by action and delivery, and we are determined to achieve the best possible agreement for the budget for 2027 together with you all. Such a budget must balance competing priorities, recognising that not everything can be prioritised while remaining accountable and responsive to the needs of our European citizens.

I am truly confident that working together, we can achieve that outcome in that timely manner. So thank you very much again today for your time, for your attention, and I look forward to the constructive engagement in the weeks ahead.

paragraphs.text: Arkadiusz Mularczyk (ECR), na piśmieBudżet Unii Europejskiej na 2027 rok powinien odpowiadać na rzeczywiste zagrożenia, a nie finansować kolejne kosztowne i ideologiczne projekty. Priorytetem musi być bezpieczeństwo: ochrona wschodniej granicy, rozwój przemysłu obronnego, mobilność wojskowa, cyberbezpieczeństwo, obrona cywilna oraz odporność infrastruktury krytycznej.Państwa wschodniej flanki, w tym Polska, ponoszą szczególne koszty ochrony całej Unii. Powinno to znaleźć odzwierciedlenie w podziale środków. Jednocześnie finansowanie nowych zadań nie może odbywać się kosztem polityki spójności, rolnictwa ani inwestycji wyrównujących różnice rozwojowe między regionami. To właśnie te polityki budują społeczną i gospodarczą odporność Europy.Budżet powinien również wzmacniać konkurencyjność europejskich przedsiębiorstw, wspierać małe i średnie firmy oraz ograniczać biurokrację. Nie można jedną ręką finansować gospodarki, a drugą obciążać jej rosnącymi kosztami energii i regulacji.Wsparcie Ukrainy pozostaje konieczne, lecz większą część kosztów jej odbudowy powinien ponieść rosyjski agresor. Unia powinna wykorzystać w tym celu zamrożone rosyjskie aktywa, zgodnie z prawem międzynarodowym.Potrzebujemy budżetu odpowiedzialnego, przejrzystego i oszczędnego — skoncentrowanego na bezpieczeństwie, rozwoju oraz równym traktowaniu wszystkich państw członkowskich, a nie na dalszej centralizacji Unii.

interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Commissioner, one month ago, the EU's new packaging rules came into effect, marking an important step towards a more circular and sustainable future for the European Union.

The packaging legislation was agreed with the objective of reducing packaging waste, bringing more recycled materials into circulation and making packaging safer for consumers. Although our institutions agreed on these rules more than two years ago, these objectives are still crucial and we remain as committed as ever to building a circular economy, as we were then.

And yet, I thank you for calling the debate today, as it brings another crucial perspective into play – the perspective of those who have to comply with the rules. Businesses all over Europe, big or small, look to us to set clear rules. Not weak rules, but simple rules. And they are right. It is important that the rules we set do not only work for environmental protection – and they must work for environmental protection – but they must work for business as well.

As Council Presidency, I can assure you that Member States are attached to this principle. We have been working on simplifying various pieces of EU legislation with exactly that purpose: to make the life of EU businesses easier without undermining environmental protection. In the legislative work done over the past years, the Council has paid particular attention to small and medium enterprises. They are the backbone of our economy. They provide jobs to 90 million people.

Now, specifically on the packaging rules, the Council is well aware of the concerns raised about the administrative burden placed on packaging producers, especially for SMEs that only produce a limited amount of packaging every year. We heard earlier of one bakery that was caught by some of these rules.

The obligation to appoint an authorised representative in up to 27 Member States may appear even more costly for very small producers with limited trade to other Member States. It is therefore appropriate to discuss whether this obligation should be adopted. There are various ways to approach this issue. For instance, exemption thresholds from the obligation to appoint an authorised representative based on national registers, or having one EU‑wide register of producers.

At the same time, let us not forget the reason why the obligation to appoint an authorised representative was introduced. The current system is set up to ensure fair competition and to avoid free‑riding. This is particularly important in the case of packaging producers from third countries, who could become nearly untraceable, if any changes to the existing regime are not carefully thought through.

To that end, we would need to find a comprehensive, systemic solution. We believe that the upcoming proposal on the Circular Economy Act is the right platform to define a well‑calibrated solution for the different waste streams. We therefore look to you, Commissioner, expecting a proposal helping to build a single market with a clear set of rules across different products and waste streams.

Only with a systemic review can we ensure a careful balance between reducing the administrative burden for EU businesses and therefore helping the creation of jobs and preserving their competitiveness, but also ensuring a level playing field with regard to third‑country producers.
I look forward to hearing what the Commission and indeed what the Members say here today.

interventions.speaker_label: Jessika Roswall, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Minister Byrne, thank you for organising this debate.

This is an important opportunity. First, to clarify some aspects of the new Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation. Second, to outline the steps that we are taking to ensure a smooth implementation and ease the burden for SMEs – from the bakers mentioned earlier to winemakers and online merchants. And thirdly, to assure you that we have listened to, and continue to listen to, a wide range of stakeholders throughout this entire journey, especially small businesses.

The Regulation was designed to cut unnecessary business costs, strengthen the circular business model, reduce our dependence on virgin resources, create a more predictable market for investments, and decrease waste – ambitious but important goals that will boost our competitiveness and protect our economy.

Designing this Regulation was not easy, and the final agreement represents a careful negotiation balance between environmental ambition and economic realities, between harmonisation and national circumstances, and between the need to transform our packaging systems on the one hand, and the capacity of businesses to adapt on the other. We should preserve that balance, but that does not mean ignoring problems that emerge during implementation. Good regulation means being ready and able to act when rules create unnecessary costs and unintended barriers. We cannot ask small companies selling small quantities across several Member States to set up authorised representatives in each national market. Hundreds of businesses have spoken to me about this issue. For some, this is forcing them to stop selling across EU and this is totally unacceptable for me. A regulation designed to strengthen the single market cannot create new barriers to participating in it, and that is why the Commission acted to provide immediate relief to these businesses. Last December, we proposed to suspend these obligations, and I really urge you to approve this proposal as quickly as possible.

More broadly, the Regulation already includes exemptions and flexibilities for smaller companies. SMEs want to rely on the documentation available from their packaging suppliers, we clarified that they can. SMEs ask to use the stocks of packaging, we told them how to do so. SMEs said they cannot be ready on day one, we allowed authorities to hold off on imposing fines. But having flexibilities on paper is not enough: it must also work in practice, and that means ensuring that businesses understand what is required of them, that Member States implement the regulation consistently, and that we intervene when unnecessary complexity emerges. We have established an expert group to give stakeholders a direct voice on implementation. We will improve practical guidance to help SMEs navigate the new rules, and we are intensifying the discussions with Member States. I also encourage national authorities to make full use of the flexibilities that are available.

We should also remember that several of the major requirements will only apply from 2030. Companies will have time to redesign packaging, adapt product lines, establish re-use systems, and invest in new recycled technologies. And we don't stop there: as part of the upcoming Circular Economy Act, we will ensure that the extended producer responsibility will work better across Europe. Here we will propose clear simplification, harmonisation and digitalisation actions to support our SMEs and our single market.

Honourable Members, this Regulation, together with the Circular Economy Act, is an essential building block of a genuine European circular economy. It holds enormous potential for Europe and for European businesses, I have no doubt of this. For European consumers, it means more protection from substances of concern, including PFAS or the so-called forever chemicals. For the single market and European businesses, it means harmonised packaging rules across Member States with less complexity and less costs. For Europe's economic resilience, it means less waste and less demand for virgin resources. It means more recycling and more re-use where it makes environmental and economic sense. And it means also new markets for circular products and materials.

So let us move forward with ambition in our objectives and pragmatism in how we achieve them. Let us work together to quickly adopt the simplification proposals that we made in the omnibus, and let us continue to identify concrete solutions to the problems on businesses encountered so we can deliver for the single market, for the environment and for European SMEs, the backbone of our economy.
This is our responsibility, but it is also, as I see it, a major opportunity, so let us grasp it together.

interventions.speaker_label: Massimiliano Salini, a nome del gruppo PPE.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, abbiamo effettivamente concluso, nella precedente legislatura, uno dei negoziati più complessi. Sono molto felice di vedere qua, oggi, insieme a noi i colleghi che hanno condiviso quella fase negoziale così articolata.

L'esito finale è buono. Ma è chiaro che adesso bisogna renderlo concretamente percorribile attraverso la fase di implementazione e, come spesso accade su regolamenti così complessi, la fase di implementazione presenta dei possibili inciampi.

Sia il ministro che la Commissaria hanno citato alcuni degli argomenti su cui questo può accadere. L'obiettivo è tutelare l'economia circolare però, al contempo, evitare il più possibile che ci siano barriere interne nel mercato europeo. Su questo secondo punto stiamo correndo dei pericoli: il caso, ad esempio, della responsabilità estesa del produttore è stato citato.

Il fatto che si individui, appunto, un rappresentante autorizzato per ognuno dei Paesi membri può essere un fatto irrilevante per le grandi compagnie ma non lo è per le piccole e medie imprese. C'è una discussione nell'omnibus sull'argomento, e io apprezzo molto, la decisione della Commissione di intervenire sull'argomento.

Io mi auguro che nel negoziato non si riduca alle micro-imprese questa revisione ma che venga esteso almeno alle medie, perché anche quelle vengono coinvolte. Oppure l'annosa questione della interpretazione del bando ex allegato V di alcuni imballaggi in plastica.

Ecco, diciamo che il negoziato parlamentare aveva generato un risultato. Io mi auguro che l'interpretazione della Commissione non lo contraddica, ad esempio, estendendo quel bando anche ai prodotti compositi nei quali sia presente una percentuale inferiore al 5% di plastica. Perché la volontà del legislatore è stata chiara e deve essere rispettata.

Vi è poi anche il tema del Consiglio, dove a volte alcuni dei punti di accordo che troviamo vengono rallentati per altri motivi. Io mi auguro, quindi, che si mantengano entrambi gli obiettivi per l'economia circolare forti in Europa e, dall'altro, una reale armonizzazione tra i 27 Paesi membri.

Vice-Président

interventions.text:
PRÉSIDENCE: YOUNOUS OMARJEE

Vice-Président

interventions.speaker_label: Delara Burkhardt, im Namen der S&D-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Frau Kommissarin! Manchmal ist es so, dass sich Kartons schneller stapeln, als die Müllabfuhr kommt. Und dann ist die Frage: Wer zahlt eigentlich für die Entsorgung? Und genau hier kommt das Prinzip der erweiterten Herstellerverantwortung ins Spiel. Die Verursacher von Abfällen sollen sich stärker an der Beseitigung dieser Abfälle finanziell beteiligen, denn sonst bleibt das bei den Kommunen bzw. bei den privaten Haushalten hängen.

Die erweiterte Herstellerverantwortung – und darum geht es hier – darf aber nicht zum Hindernis für den Binnenmarkt werden. Der europäische Binnenmarkt ist eine der größten Errungenschaften der europäischen Integration, und er muss eben genau – besonders für die kleinen Unternehmen − funktionieren.

Mir hat ein Hersteller von elektronischen Musikinstrumenten aus Leipzig geschrieben. Er hat neun Beschäftigte, liefert in 20 Ländern in der EU. Fixkosten für die Registrierung und Benennung von Bevollmächtigten in diesen Ländern für seine Verpackungen sind jährlich ungefähr 5 000 EUR. Dabei schickt er teilweise nur bis zu vier Pakete in diese 20 Länder. Dieser Leipziger Musikinstrumentehändler will Verantwortung für seine Verpackungen übernehmen; das hat er mir geschrieben. Aber er kann schlicht und einfach keine 20 nationalen Systeme bespielen. Er wird daher als Konsequenz Länder aus seinem Shop rausnehmen müssen; das ist ein Verlust für den Händler, aber es ist vor allen Dingen auch ein Verlust für die Vielfalt in unserem Binnenmarkt und für uns als Verbraucherinnen und Verbraucher.

Ein fairer Binnenmarkt sieht anders aus. Regeln müssen so gestaltet sein, dass kleine europäische Unternehmen grenzüberschreitend tätig sein können und nicht strukturell gegenüber großen Plattformen benachteiligt werden. Dafür brauchen wir die erweiterte Herstellerverantwortung – aber eben europäisch. Die Abschaffung der Bevollmächtigtenpflicht im grenzüberschreitenden Handel ist deswegen nur ein erster Schritt.
Wir brauchen einen größeren Wurf über das Kreislaufwirtschaftsgesetz, einen europäischen digitalen One‑Stop‑Shop – und nicht 27 nationale Bürokratien.

Wir brauchen einen größeren Wurf über das Kreislaufwirtschaftsgesetz, einen europäischen digitalen One‑Stop‑Shop – und nicht 27 nationale Bürokratien.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Anne-Sophie Frigout, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, votre règlement relatif aux emballages et aux déchets d’emballages est une immondice bureaucratique de plus, made in Bruxelles. Au nom de l'écologie, vous imposez à toutes nos PME et micro-entreprises de s'enregistrer dans chaque pays de l'Union européenne pour désigner un mandataire. 27 formulaires, et à chaque fois, cela représente entre 600 et 2 000 € de frais par an. Pour un caviste, un éditeur, un artisan français, c'est tout simplement la mort de l'export.

Et qui paiera la facture? Le consommateur, parce qu'au bout du compte, ces frais, ce sont toujours les prix qui les absorbent. Et le pire est que vous avez avoué avoir demandé aux États de ne pas appliquer vos règles, de ne pas sanctionner les entreprises. Parce que ce texte est, je cite, clairement disproportionné. Vous l'avez rédigé, vous l'avez voté et vous demandez vous-même de ne pas l'appliquer. Un comble!
Alors arrêtez l'hypocrisie. Abrogez ce texte, rendez aux États et à nos entreprises la liberté d'entreprendre, et cessez vos mesures d'écologie punitive.

interventions.speaker_label: Ana Vasconcelos, on behalf of the Renew Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, the ideal of the single market is that anyone in a Member State can sell across all 27 Member States without borders.

I can only imagine the perplexity of so many Europeans with small businesses, when they realised in the middle of August that yet another bureaucratic barrier was raised for them to operate in the single market. Realising that it is now easier to sell outside of the EU for them than inside of the EU. And just in the past month alone, since these rules came into force, several businesses announced they were cancelling their shipping orders or shutting down their businesses altogether. This is simply unacceptable for the EU.
Even more perplexing is that the Commission saw this coming and tried to stop it, and Parliament is broadly supportive of its initiative to do so, of suspending these rules.
So what is really perplexing is that Council refused initially to negotiate. Now we asked, as parliamentarians, a group of us, if Council wants to reconsider its position.
(The President interrupted the speaker)

We have seen hopeful signs from some Member States that they are moving in that direction. And my appeal is that we deliver fast. The circular economy cannot come at the cost of the single market, and surely not at the cost of hardworking Europeans.
