Madam President, honourable Members, the European Union and Zambia share a robust partnership based on a commitment to multilateralism and the rules-based international order. The EU's partnership with Zambia is also vibrant under the Global Gateway and Lobito Corridor. Zambia is a stable and constructive partner, aligned with the EU on regional and global issues, including Ukraine.

The EU was invited to observe the recent general elections, and I welcome and thank Parliament for its role in that regard. I also thank the Chief Observer, Mr McNamara, and the head of the EPP delegation, Mr Lopatka, for their collaboration.

The atmosphere around the elections was clearly tense. The Election Observation Mission detected irregularities and shortcomings, including in counting and appeals processes. The mission will present its final report soon, with recommendations to strengthen future electoral processes. The EU delegation will follow up and the EU stands ready to support electoral reforms in Zambia.

In this context, we note with concern the death of former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya during a police operation and the arrest of opposition figures. The main opposition candidate and other opposition members are currently detained on charges of treason and sedition. We have raised our concerns with the authorities in Lusaka and call for a transparent investigation into the incidents that led to Mr Kafwaya's death. Our ambassador is following developments closely.

While national security is important, accountability for disproportionate or arbitrary use of force is necessary to rebuild the trust. Furthermore, allegations of criminal conduct must be addressed with respect for a fair trial and a transparent judicial process.

Our position remains one of principled partnership based on Zambia's international commitments as well as obligations under international human rights law. Zambia has built an international reputation for democratic governance and political stability, and should stand by those principles. We trust that the Zambian authorities will find a path towards reconciliation and dialogue by safeguarding political pluralism, media freedom and civic space.

The EU should remain Zambia's partner of choice while upholding the fundamental values of democratic governance, rule of law and respect for human rights.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam Vice-President, honourable Members, Commissioner Lahbib, let me first express our deepest condolences and full solidarity with the people of Nepal and all others concerned after the devastating flood disaster that took place on 26 August.

It is hard to imagine, but 1 300 people have lost their lives, over 6 000 people have been injured – numerous European citizens amongst them – and an estimated 15 000 houses were destroyed. Our thoughts are with every family impacted by this tragedy in and beyond Nepal.

The European Union stands ready to help through this incredibly difficult time of mourning, recovering and rebuilding. There are obvious and urgent humanitarian needs, including the provision of clean water, health and shelter. Accessing those in need and coordinating support efforts are key challenges. The European Union released EUR 2.5 million in new emergency funding in response to the disaster. These funds came on top of the EUR 2.9 million in disaster preparedness funding that was already allocated to Nepal at the beginning of this year.

Beyond funding, we also provided rapid operational support: we organised a humanitarian air bridge flight with vital relief supplies to the affected areas. Our technical teams were immediately sent to assess the scale of the disaster and advise on rescue efforts using Copernicus satellite mapping and analytical support from the Joint Research Centre. Indeed, we triggered the EU's Civil Protection Mechanism. Offers of in-kind assistance from six Member States and Norway are now accepted and arriving in Nepal.

The European Union remains in close coordination with the Nepalese authorities, EU Member States and international partners to assess the impact and support recovery, remediation and reconstruction efforts in the aftermath of the disaster in the medium and long term.

Nepal is among the world's most vulnerable countries to natural disasters, so we must learn from this disaster and continue to work with Nepal towards supporting climate resilience. Although scientific accounts of the actual trigger of the disaster differ, it is highly likely that global warming played its part. So, in line with the principle of climate justice, the EU and its Member States, as the biggest contributors of the international climate finance, have been supporting mitigation and adaptation measures in developing and most vulnerable countries.
We will do our utmost to support Nepal in dealing with the consequences of this unprecedented event.

interventions.speaker_label: Hadja Lahbib, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, the flash floods in Nepal have caused a devastating loss of life and widespread destruction. Our thoughts are first and foremost with those who have lost families and loved ones, who are still searching for them among the many still missing people, and with all the brave responders providing emergency support on the ground.

We are in regular contact with the Nepalese authorities, whose response has been and continues to be deeply impressive. The very same has to be said about the Nepalese Red Cross, who have done outstanding work since the first hours of this crisis. The European Union also responded very fast. We quickly mobilised EUR 2.5 million in emergency humanitarian assistance. This funding supports immediate assistance, including healthcare, clean water, sanitation, food, shelter and protection for the most vulnerable. We have also been sending flights to Nepal, delivering critical relief material from our warehouses in Copenhagen and Kuala Lumpur. Our EU humanitarian air bridges have now brought over 150 metric tonnes of aid to the country, and we will continue with further flights already scheduled.

Nepal has also activated the EU civil protection mechanism, officially requesting help from European countries. Six EU Member States, as well as Norway, are providing assistance through our EU mechanism, donating medical items, body bags, hygiene kits, emergency energy equipment and much more. And because logistics and coordination can be one of the biggest challenges during a crisis, we have also sent European experts on the ground to assist the Nepalese authorities in making sure the response is efficient and well designed for both the immediate and the long-term needs of the affected communities.

Furthermore, we continue to provide technical expertise through our Copernicus satellite emergency management services. Copernicus was activated on the very day of the floods, and it continues to produce maps that provide responders with vital information, such as the extent of damage to roads, bridges, airports, power stations, and other critical infrastructure.

Honourable Members, our support to Nepal did not begin with the emergency. Nepal is one of the country's most exposed to natural hazards and to the growing consequences of climate change. Therefore, at the beginning of the year, even before these devastating floods, the European Union had committed almost EUR 3 million to disaster preparedness in Nepal. This helped our humanitarian partners on the ground to respond immediately once the flash floods had hit. Investments in disaster preparedness are key. Both at home and abroad. We cannot prevent every extreme event, but with better preparedness, stronger local response capacity and effective early warning systems, we can greatly reduce their impact and human cost.

Nepal will face significant challenges as it moves from immediate emergency response to recovery and reconstruction. The European Union will remain closely engaged with the Nepalese authorities, our humanitarian and development partners and the wider international community to support this work. The EU delegation in Kathmandu plays a vital role in this on the ground.

Honourable Members, when an earthquake struck Nepal in 2015, Europe was there. Eleven years later, Europe is there again. But what matters just as much is that we have also been there for all these years in between, investing in preparedness, working with local partners and helping to strengthen the capacity to respond. That is what being a reliable partner and friend means: not simply responding when a crisis strikes, but preparing before it does.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, ničivé záplavy v oblasti Nepálu si vyžádaly více než patnáct set lidských životů a stále je několik tisíc lidí pohřešovaných. Celé rodiny přišly o své domovy, místní komunity o základní infrastrukturu a mnoho lidí stále čeká na zprávy o svých blízkých.

V první řadě bych chtěl jako člověk, který byl dvakrát na pozorovatelské misi v Nepálu, vyjádřit svou skutečnou upřímnou soustrast rodinám a pozůstalým. Oceňuji rychlou reakci Komise, to bylo perfektní. Myslím, že v podobě finanční a humanitární pomoci v této oblasti jsme byli jedni z prvních, kteří nabídli, že můžeme dále Nepálu pomáhat. Zároveň však nesmíme přehlížet Čínou spravovanou část Tibetu, kde žádné informace nemáme a kde nevíme, jakým způsobem se dostala pomoc tamním obyvatelům.

Evropská unie není v tomto regionu pouze vzdáleným pozorovatelem. My tam investujeme. Předtím jsme tam investovali přes dvě stě milionů, dnes máme dalších sto třináct milionů na období 2025 až 2027. A proto bychom se v naší pomoci měli zaměřit na systémy včasného varování, sdílení meteorologických dat, monitoring ledovců a přeshraniční krizovou komunikaci. Pevně věřím, že společně se nám do budoucna podaří zachránit více životů lidí v Nepálu.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Sandra Gómez López, en nombre del Grupo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, en primer lugar, desde el Grupo Socialista queremos trasladar nuestro más sentido pésame a las familias de las víctimas y toda nuestra solidaridad con el pueblo de Nepal.

Esta tragedia —que ya lleva más de 1 300 fallecidos y más de 6 000 desaparecidos y desaparecidas— nos está recordando una profunda injusticia climática. Nepal apenas ha contribuido a las emisiones globales, pero, en cambio, está sufriendo algunas de las consecuencias más graves del cambio climático. El calentamiento y el retroceso de los glaciares están aumentando los riesgos que afrontan las comunidades del Himalaya.

Y quienes más hemos contribuido históricamente a ese cambio climático tenemos también una responsabilidad mayor: creo, sinceramente, que lo podemos hacer mejor. Es indiscutible que Europa ha ayudado y ha sido solidaria con Nepal, pero los 2,5 millones de euros que hemos dado en ayuda humanitaria se quedan cortos frente a todo lo que podemos hacer como europeos y europeas teniendo en cuenta nuestra responsabilidad.

Por eso, Europa debe estar presente, hoy, en emergencia, pero también mañana, apoyando la reconstrucción, adaptación, sistemas de alerta temprana y una infraestructura más resiliente. Porque la solidaridad no es solo acudir después de una catástrofe, sino también ayudar a prevenir la siguiente.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Şerban Dimitrie Sturdza, au nom du groupe ECR.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, en quelques heures des communautés entières au Népal ont été dévastées. Plus de 1 400 personnes ont perdu la vie et plus de 5 000 sont toujours portées disparues. Des milliers de familles ont perdu leurs proches, leurs maisons et parfois tout ce qu'elles avaient construit.

En tant que président de la délégation du Parlement pour les relations avec les pays d'Asie du Sud, j'ai demandé ce débat car le Népal doit savoir qu'il n'est pas seul. Je salue la réponse rapide et solidaire de l'Europe: 2,5 millions d'euros d'aide humanitaire d'urgence, 82 tonnes de matériel de première nécessité ainsi que le soutien satellitaire de Copernicus.

Mais notre responsabilité ne s'arrête pas à l'urgence. Le Népal aura besoin de notre soutien pour se relever, reconstruire et mieux résister aux catastrophes éventuelles à l'avenir. Aujourd'hui, notre message au peuple népalais est clair: l'Europe est à vos côtés dans le deuil, dans le relèvement et dans la reconstruction.

interventions.speaker_label: Grégory Allione, au nom du groupe Renew.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, n'oublions pas que les premières victimes du changement climatique sont souvent celles qui ont le moins contribué. Je pense aux territoires ultramarins, les états insulaires, les régions montagneuses, et le Népal en est aujourd'hui l'exemple le plus tragique. 1 400 décédés, 5 600 personnes toujours portées disparues, et derrière ces chiffres, ce sont des familles brisées et tout un pays à reconstruire. Et ce soir, effectivement, nous pensons à toutes les victimes, à leurs familles auxquelles on adresse toute notre solidarité.

Ne croyons pas que ce qui est arrivé au Népal ne peut pas arriver chez nous. Et je me demande parfois pourquoi certains restent encore climatosceptiques. Il n'y a qu'à regarder nos montagnes, il n'y a qu'à discuter avec ceux qui y vivent. Regardez la fonte des glaciers cet été. J'étais cet été, Madame la Commissaire, à Chamonix et j'ai discuté avec les maires du secteur. Ils sont inquiets et ils ont, eux, l'humilité de se sentir concernés.

Alors je voulais vous remercier pour préparer justement un exercice d'ampleur dans les Alpes prochainement, au mois de mars 2027, où nous allons préparer finalement ces événements qui peuvent arriver dans nos Alpes, dans nos montagnes. Nous avons le pouvoir et le devoir de nous préparer au pire, et nous devons surtout empêcher que le pire devienne la norme.

interventions.text:
Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, n'oublions pas que les premières victimes du changement climatique sont souvent celles qui ont le moins contribué. Je pense aux territoires ultramarins, les états insulaires, les régions montagneuses, et le Népal en est aujourd'hui l'exemple le plus tragique. 1 400 décédés, 5 600 personnes toujours portées disparues, et derrière ces chiffres, ce sont des familles brisées et tout un pays à reconstruire. Et ce soir, effectivement, nous pensons à toutes les victimes, à leurs familles auxquelles on adresse toute notre solidarité.

Ne croyons pas que ce qui est arrivé au Népal ne peut pas arriver chez nous. Et je me demande parfois pourquoi certains restent encore climatosceptiques. Il n'y a qu'à regarder nos montagnes, il n'y a qu'à discuter avec ceux qui y vivent. Regardez la fonte des glaciers cet été. J'étais cet été, Madame la Commissaire, à Chamonix et j'ai discuté avec les maires du secteur. Ils sont inquiets et ils ont, eux, l'humilité de se sentir concernés.

Alors je voulais vous remercier pour préparer justement un exercice d'ampleur dans les Alpes prochainement, au mois de mars 2027, où nous allons préparer finalement ces événements qui peuvent arriver dans nos Alpes, dans nos montagnes. Nous avons le pouvoir et le devoir de nous préparer au pire, et nous devons surtout empêcher que le pire devienne la norme.

interventions.speaker_label: Marie Toussaint, au nom du groupe Verts/ALE.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, 1 400 morts, plus de 5 000 disparus, des cercueils enterrés vides. Le 26 août dernier, un pan de glacier s'est détaché et a rayé des villages entiers de la carte du Népal. Mais soyons clairs, le Népal ne réchauffe pas la planète; il paie pourtant le prix fort du dérèglement climatique. Des milliers de vies et 10 % de son PIB.

Alors on nous dira qu'on ne saura jamais attribuer une catastrophe à un coupable précis. Mais les glaciers de l'Himalaya ne s'effondrent pas par hasard: ils s'effondrent parce que nos États, les plus riches, ont brûlé du charbon, du pétrole et du gaz pendant plus de deux siècles. Parce que des gouvernements – nos gouvernements – ont soutenu le déploiement des énergies fossiles pour le profit d'un tout petit nombre. La droite de cet hémicycle prétend souvent qu'il suffit de dire que nous ne sommes plus les seuls à polluer la planète et que cela balayerait toute responsabilité. Notre dette climatique, elle est historique, elle est présente et personne, non personne ne l'a jamais réglée.

Alors écoutons la jeunesse népalaise qui nous dit: «On veut que les responsables payent». Ces responsables, nous les connaissons. Ce sont les multinationales fossiles qui continuent à forer de nouveaux puits de pétrole et de gaz après avoir menti pendant plusieurs décennies sur les impacts de leurs activités. Combien de vallées encore englouties avant que les dirigeants ne soient enfin placés devant leurs responsabilités?

interventions.speaker_label: Hadja Lahbib, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, first of all, thank you for underlining the specific situation that Tibet is in. We must not overlook the situation in Tibet. I totally agree. We need to have reliable and timely information. It is essential. It supports search and rescue, enables families to obtain information and allows also responders to identify the needs. So yes, we would like to see more clarity and transparency on what is happening there.

Nepal, when it comes to climate change, is one of the most affected countries by natural hazards, although it is not one of the most contributors to population, and that is why preparedness is so important, and that is why we invested almost EUR 3 million before this crisis hit.

But of course, preparedness is not a substitute for climate action or climate finance. It's about protecting lives. Extreme events are becoming more severe, and vulnerable communities like the Nepalese are often the least equipped to withstand them. Investing in early warning systems, local response capacity and disaster preparedness can make the difference between an incident and a humanitarian catastrophe.

You may know that Nepal has requested support from the fund for responding to loss and damage. This system has its own governance and arrangements. The procedures for considering requests for support is ongoing, and the European Commission currently has a seat on the board among 26 Member States and is part of the process of responding to the first funding requests, including from Nepal. The European Commission has pledged EUR 25 million to this fund.

interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Commissioner Hadja Lahbib, as has been stated here by all of the honourable Members, the natural disaster in Nepal caused immense devastation, leaving many communities shattered and families in mourning. And we express again our full solidarity with those affected.

In response, the European Union has moved with rapid action and solidarity, delivering substantial support. And that is what we are about as a European Union. That is why we need to maintain this type of work around the world as best as we can, because it is so important to help those suffering. But it also is a means of projecting what the European Union is about around the world.
The Member States of the European Union are closely following developments, and of course, will respond to Nepal's requests for further help as necessary.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, stimați colegi, România are cea mai lungă frontieră terestră și maritimă cu Ucraina. Consecința directă a acestei granițe o reprezintă 46 de pătrunderi neautorizate în spațiul aerian românesc, de la începutul războiului și până astăzi.

Pentru că trebuie să vorbim mai mult despre apărarea antidronă a flancului estic, trebuie să recunoaștem efortul făcut de statele de pe flancul estic și să lucrăm împreună pentru a fi mai puternici, fără costuri enorme.

Este urgent ca România să investească inteligent în capabilități de detectare și interceptare a dronelor, dar și în capacitatea de a conduce, nu doar de a urma inițiativele de apărare ale flancului estic.

De aceea am votat pentru acest raport în plen. Statele membre au nevoie de mai puțină birocrație când vine vorba despre investiții în apărare și de o industrie capabilă să inoveze și să producă mai repede la o scară mai mare.

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, η ομιλία της Προέδρου της Επιτροπής ομολογεί τον στόχο για μια θηριώδη πολεμική βιομηχανία που περνά μέσα και από το προωθούμενο πακέτο απλοποιήσεων, το οποίο προκλητικά εντάσσεται στον τομέα της άμυνας. Αυτό παρέχει ασυλία στους ομίλους με a priori αδειοδοτήσεις, fast track διαδικασίες και ελευθερία μεταφορών όπλων και πυρομαχικών από άκρη σε άκρη σε όλη την Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση. Πάνω από όλα, προβλέπει πακέτα στήριξης ύψους εκατοντάδων δισεκατομμυρίων για την πολεμική βιομηχανία, που ήδη έχει εκτοξευθεί κατά 80% την τελευταία πενταετία. Προβλέπει επίσης πριμοδότηση-μαμούθ του αντιδραστικού καθεστώτος Zelenskyy με χρήμα και αμερικανικούς Patriot. Η μεθόδευση αλλαγών στο άρθρο 42.7 —το λεγόμενο Ευρωπαϊκό Συμβούλιο Ασφάλειας— σε συμμαχία με τον Καναδά και άλλες τρίτες χώρες, όπως και η ευρωενωσιακή εκδοχή του άρθρου 4 του ΝΑΤΟ, προδίδουν ότι η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση συγκροτεί μηχανισμούς κήρυξης πολέμου απέναντι στα ανταγωνιστικά της ιμπεριαλιστικά κέντρα και πάνω από όλα σε βάρος των λαών. Καμία εμπλοκή, καμία θυσία για την πολεμική οικονομία. Αυξήσεις σε μισθούς, υγεία, παιδεία, πολιτική προστασία.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, am votat în favoarea acestui raport pentru că Europa poate, și trebuie, să producă în vederea propriei apărări, mai repede și mai mult în ceea ce privește propria-și apărare.

Avem însă o problemă: pe de o parte, comisarul pe apărare vine și ne propune genul acesta de Omnibus, să modificăm legi pentru a îmbunătăți tot ceea ce înseamnă producția în domeniul apărării, pe de altă parte, Ursula von der Leyen și alți comisari vin cu genul de reglementări privind decarbonizarea, care distrug industria de apărare.

E important și pentru acest Parlament să decidă ce vrea: dorește industrie în Europa și, dacă dorește industrie în Europa, trebuie să dereglementeze, adică să elimine toate aceste reglementări care au condus deja la creșterea prețului energiei, costului de producție și eliminarea companiilor din Europa, sau să rămână în aceeași ideologie ca până acum să alunge industria de aici.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, stimați colegi, războiul acestei ere nu începe neapărat cu tancuri. Poate să înceapă cu o dronă care intră în spațiul aerian, cu un atac cibernetic asupra unei rețele energetice sau cu bruiajul comunicațiilor.

Liderii noștri trebuie să înțeleagă că vremea certurilor politice a trecut. Acum trebuie să facem ceva ce contează mai mult: să ne ținem cetățenii în siguranță. Trebuie să ne concentrăm pe apărarea infrastructurii energetice, a porturilor, transporturilor și telecomunicațiilor.

Pentru că într-un război hibrid, arătatul cu degetul nu apără pe nimeni de o pană generalizată de curent, de un port blocat sau de un atac cibernetic care paralizează un serviciu public de maximă necesitate.
De aceea am votat în favoarea acestui raport. Avem nevoie de state pregătite și de suveranitate militară în Europa.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, esta mañana, en el debate sobre el estado de la Unión, la presidenta Von der Leyen ha hablado de proteger la integridad y la seguridad de la Unión Europea contra los ataques híbridos y ha hecho una referencia a la crisis en Ceuta, anunciando un mecanismo de emergencia que no puede concretarse en un endurecimiento de los procedimientos de retorno sin garantías; sino que debería concretarse en inversión en los países de origen y tránsito, creando oportunidades, y la apertura, por fin, de vías legales que sean capaces de desactivar el modelo de negocio de los tráficos ilícitos.

Pero, fundamentalmente, lo que es imprescindible es que la Unión Europea haga honor a su promesa de ser globalmente relevante como actor geopolítico. Eso exige que la Unión Europea sea capaz de hablar con una voz respetable, madurando de una vez en su política exterior y superando la regla de la unanimidad. Y una ocasión excelente es esa Conferencia sobre el Futuro de Europa anunciada con motivo del 70 aniversario del Tratado de Roma. Superar la unanimidad es imprescindible para que la Unión Europea madure definitivamente.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Rezolucja dotyczy wojny hybrydowej oraz ochrony integralności terytorialnej Unii Europejskiej i infrastruktury krytycznej niezbędnej dla bezpieczeństwa i obrony. Głosowałem za przyjęciem tej rezolucji, ponieważ wojna hybrydowa nie jest już zagrożeniem teoretycznym. Polska i inne państwa wschodniej flanki NATO mierzą się z cyberatakami, sabotażem, dezinformacją i instrumentalizacją migracji oraz atakami na infrastrukturę krytyczną.

Europa dlatego musi wzmocnić swoją granicę, sieci energetyczne, korytarze transportowe i systemy cyfrowe. Działanie Unii powinny wspierać państwa członkowskie, uzupełniać NATO, ale nie powielać ich zadań i kompetencji. Unia musi przeznaczyć znacznie większe środki na wschodnią flankę, mobilność wojskową, infrastrukturę podwójnego zastosowania, ochronę lotnisk.
Europejska solidarność musi oznaczać konkretne inwestycje, zdolności operacyjne oraz stanowczą odpowiedź na każdy atak hybrydowy na Unię Europejską.

Unia musi przeznaczyć znacznie większe środki na wschodnią flankę, mobilność wojskową, infrastrukturę podwójnego zastosowania, ochronę lotnisk.

Europejska solidarność musi oznaczać konkretne inwestycje, zdolności operacyjne oraz stanowczą odpowiedź na każdy atak hybrydowy na Unię Europejską.
